definition_zh: 装备；配备（尤指军装军械）
definition_en: to equip or dress someone, especially a soldier, with the needed gear
core_image: 军械库前的配装台：一件件扣上腰带与弹药盒
scene: 黎明前的新兵列队，军士逐件为他扣上装具，直到镜中的人像样起来。 The quartermaster will accouter the recruits before drill.
sceneCN: 这里 accouter 是「装备、配备」（第 1 个义项：给军人配齐装具）；句意为军需官将在操练前为新兵配装。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「装具；服饰装备」
由本词加过去分词后缀构成（英式拼写 accoutred），义为「配备装具的」

senses.title: To equip a soldier with gear
senses.definition: to provide someone, especially a soldier, with weapons, armour, and clothing
senses.definitionCN: 给某人（尤指军人）配发武器、盔甲与服装
senses.example: The armoury accoutered each guard before his watch began.
senses.exampleCN: 军械库在每名卫兵上岗前为其配装。
senses.why: The French source meant to sew onto a garment, and outfitting a soldier is adding one piece of gear after another to the body.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义是缝到衣服上；为士兵配装正是把一件件装具「缀」到身体上。

senses.title: To dress in a distinctive way
senses.definition: to clothe or adorn someone in a particular, often elaborate, style
senses.definitionCN: 以某种特定且常显考究的方式为某人着装打扮
senses.example: Guards were accoutered in ceremonial red and gold.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵们被装点在仪式化的红金制服中。
senses.why: If a soldier can be covered with equipment, a courtier can be covered with finery; the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 士兵可以被装具覆盖，廷臣也可以被华服覆盖；同一个动词兼顾两者。

intro.en: Accouter comes from Old French accoutrer, perhaps from cousture 'sewing', with earlier parts uncertain.
intro.cn: accouter 来自古法语 accoutrer，可能源于 cousture（缝纫），更早的成分来源不确定。

items.en: consuere meant to sew together, a likely ancestor via reconstruction.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 consuere（缝合）可能是其重构的源头。

items.en: cousture meant a seam or sewing.
items.cn: 古法语 cousture 意为针脚、缝纫。

items.en: accoutrer meant to sew on, then to dress someone up.
items.cn: 古法语 accoutrer 意为缝上，后指为人装扮。

items.en: English accoutre first served military outfitting.
items.cn: 英语 accoutre 最初用于军队配装。

items.en: American spelling accouter and British accoutre coexist.
items.cn: 美式拼写 accouter 与英式 accoutre 并存。

note.en: The first group gathers the sewing-root family and spelling variants; the second gathers words for equipping.
note.cn: 第一组收缝纫词根词族与拼写变体；第二组收表示装备的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same verb.
The gear itself, as a noun.
High fashion sewing, from the same French sewing word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指高级定制缝纫。

entries.definition: To supply with what is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「配备所需之物」。

entries.definition: To provide a full set of gear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「配齐全套装备」。

entries.definition: To dress in fine or ordered clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 文学化动词，义为「盛装装扮」。

entries.definition: To clothe, especially finely.
entries.definitionCN: 正式动词，义为「着装；盛饰」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the sewing story and the spelling twins; the abstract hooks picture the armoury table.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用缝纫典故与拼写孪生词；抽象记忆点想象军械库的配装台。

normal.en: The French source meant to sew onto a garment.
normal.cn: 法语原义是缝到衣服上。

normal.en: Couture, high sewing, shares the same sewing root.
normal.cn: couture（高级缝纫）共享同一缝纫词根。

normal.en: British spelling drops the extra e-r: accoutre.
normal.cn: 英式拼写少一个 e-r：accoutre。

normal.en: The noun accouterment means the gear itself.
normal.cn: 名词 accouterment 指装具本身。

normal.en: Military contexts keep the word alive today.
normal.cn: 军事语境让这个词沿用至今。

abstract.en: Picture a sergeant buckling straps on a recruit, one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象军士长为新兵逐一扣上背带。

abstract.en: Picture a tailor sewing buckles straight onto a uniform.
abstract.cn: 想象裁缝把扣环直接缝上制服。

abstract.en: Picture a knight shining head to toe before the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象骑士在城门前从头到脚全副武装。

examples.en: The museum accoutered the mannequin with a genuine cavalry kit.
examples.cn: 博物馆为人体模型配上了真正的骑兵装具。

examples.en: Pages were accoutered in silk before the coronation.
examples.cn: 加冕礼前，侍从们被装点在丝绸之中。

examples.en: Historians study how seventeenth-century armies accoutered their foot soldiers.
examples.cn: 历史学家研究十七世纪的军队如何为步兵配装。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库特」——把装备「库」里的一件件「特」快配上身。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 consuere（缝合）→ 古法语 cousture（缝）→ accoutrer（缝上；装扮）→ 英语 accouter（配装）

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from military outfitting piece by piece, to dressing in a distinctive style.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从逐件配发军装军械，扩展到以特定风格盛装打扮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fastening one piece of gear onto a body
core.cn: 核心意象：把一件件装具「缀」上身体

branches.en: Gear attached to a soldier until ready.
branches.cn: 装具一件件上身，直至战备。

branches.en: Finery attached for show instead of war.
branches.cn: 为仪态而非战斗披挂的华服。

branches.en: Both senses share the sewing-on picture.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享「缝上、缀上」的画面。

branches.en: The verb implies completeness of the kit.
branches.cn: 该动词暗示装具的齐全。

branches.en: Ceremony and parade keep the elaborate sense alive.
branches.cn: 仪式与阅兵保留着考究装扮的义项。

intro.en: The word joins a toward-prefix with the sewing stem and a verb ending; the family adds a gear noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由「向」前缀、「缝纫」词干与动词结尾组成；词族另派生装具名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuere is a reconstructed ancestor, so the Latin entry is marked as likely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consuere 是重构的祖先，拉丁条目按「可能来源」标注。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「装具；服饰装备」
形容词，义为「配备装具的」

definition_zh: 伴奏者；伴奏员
definition_en: a musician who plays music to support a singer or another performer
core_image: 琴凳上的托举者：让主唱站上光亮的中心
scene: 彩排室里她翻着乐谱，目光始终追着歌手的呼吸。 The rehearsal pianist served as the choir's accompanist for ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 accompanist 是「伴奏者」（第 1 个义项：为他人演奏托举性音乐的人）；句意为这位排练钢琴师担任合唱团伴奏十年。

collocations.phrase: the official accompanist of the competition

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「陪伴；伴奏」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「伴奏」

senses.title: A musician who supports another performer
senses.definition: a player, often a pianist, who provides the supporting music for a lead performer
senses.definitionCN: 为领唱或主奏者提供支撑音乐的乐手，常为钢琴师
senses.example: The accompanist followed the singer's every pause.
senses.exampleCN: 伴奏者紧随着歌手的每一次停顿。
senses.why: The suffix -ist names a person who does the act, so the word names the one who plays the accompaniment.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ist 标记做某一行为的人，所以这个词指演奏伴奏的人。

senses.title: A helpful partner in music-making
senses.definition: any musician who supports the ensemble, such as a rehearsal pianist for a choir or a dance class
senses.definitionCN: 泛指支撑整个排演的音乐家，如为合唱团、舞蹈课弹伴奏的排练琴师
senses.example: The dance school hired a full-time accompanist last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这所舞蹈学校去年聘请了全职伴奏。
senses.why: Beyond the concert stage, anyone whose art is playing under others, in studios and classrooms, earns the same name.
senses.whyCN: 走出音乐厅，凡在琴房与教室里以托举他人为艺的乐手，都配得上这个称谓。

intro.en: Accompanist adds the person suffix -ist to accompany, whose Latin root companio meant one who shares bread.
intro.cn: accompanist 在 accompany 之上加「人」后缀 -ist，其拉丁词根 companio 意为分食面包的人。

items.en: companio meant one who shares bread, panis being bread.
items.cn: companio 意为分享面包之人，panis 即面包。

items.en: compaignon meant one who travels with another.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 意为同行者。

items.en: The verb meant to go along with, later to play along with.
items.cn: 动词意为伴随，后指配乐陪奏。

items.en: French used accompanateur for the supporting player.
items.cn: 法语用 accompanateur 指伴奏乐手。

items.en: English formed accompanist with its own -ist suffix.
items.cn: 英语用自有的 -ist 后缀造出 accompanist。

note.en: The first group gathers the companion word family; the second gathers names for supporting musicians.
note.cn: 第一组收 companion 词族；第二组收指辅助乐手的称谓。

entries.definition: The music the accompanist plays.
entries.definitionCN: 同根名词，指伴奏者奏出的音乐。

entries.definition: The base verb of the family.
A partner in crime; spelling-similar, different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指同谋；仅拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: A longer phrase for the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，指同一角色的较长说法。

entries.definition: A band member supporting the lead, in jazz usage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，爵士乐用语，指辅助主奏的乐手。

entries.definition: The featured performer the accompanist supports.
entries.definitionCN: 对照名词，指伴奏者所托举的主奏者。

entries.definition: One who directs rather than accompanies a choir.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指指挥而非伴奏合唱团的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the -ist person suffix and the shared-bread root; the abstract hooks picture the patient player.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「人」后缀 -ist 与「分面包」词根；抽象记忆点想象耐心的琴师。

normal.en: -ist marks a person: accompanist is the one who accompanies.
normal.cn: -ist 标记人：accompanist 就是做伴奏的人。

normal.en: Compare artist and violinist for the same pattern.
normal.cn: 类比 artist、violinist，同一构词模式。

normal.en: The word hides accompany plus the -ist tail.
normal.cn: 词内藏着 accompany 加 -ist 尾。

normal.en: Most accompanists are pianists in practice.
normal.cn: 实践中伴奏者多为钢琴师。

normal.en: The plural is accompanists.
normal.cn: 复数为 accompanists。

abstract.en: Picture a pianist watching the singer, not the keys.
abstract.cn: 想象盯着歌手而非琴键的琴师。

abstract.en: Picture a helper lifting a friend onto a stage.
abstract.cn: 想象把友人托上舞台的帮手。

abstract.en: Picture bread shared quietly before the concert begins.
abstract.cn: 想象音乐会开场前静静分享的面包。

examples.en: The young accompanist sight-read the entire sonata without error.
examples.cn: 年轻的伴奏者毫无差错地视奏了整首奏鸣曲。

examples.en: Every competitor may bring a personal accompanist.
examples.cn: 每位选手都可以自带伴奏。

examples.en: A good accompanist listens more than plays.
examples.cn: 优秀的伴奏者听多于奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿坎帕尼斯特」——同伴里最「斯特」（厉害）的那个，专门为别人伴奏。

root: 拉丁语 com-（共同）+ panis（面包）→ companio → accompany（伴奏）+ -ist（人）→ accompanist（伴奏者）

sensesIntro.en: The word has one focused sense: the musician whose art is supporting another performer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词义项集中：指以托举他人表演为艺的乐手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the player who makes someone else shine
core.cn: 核心意象：让别人发光的演奏者

branches.en: The pianist or player under the lead performer.
branches.cn: 居于主唱主奏之下的琴师或乐手。

branches.en: Choosing to stay in the shadow by choice.
branches.cn: 甘愿退居暗影的选择。

branches.en: Listening is the first skill of this person.
branches.cn: 倾听是这种人的第一技艺。

branches.en: The role completes the performance rather than rivals it.
branches.cn: 这个角色成全演出而非与之争锋。

branches.en: The shared-bread origin keeps the humble partnership alive.
branches.cn: 「分面包」的词源让谦逊的伙伴关系延续至今。

intro.en: The word joins the accompany stem with the person suffix -ist.
intro.cn: 这个词由 accompany 词干加「人」后缀 -ist 构成。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin companio is the deep root, so the Latin entry records the bread-sharing word.
latinIntro.cn: 后期拉丁语 companio 是深远词根，拉丁条目记录这个「分面包」的词。

definition_zh: 红树林；红树林森林；热带与亚热带潮间带林地；红树林生态系统
definition_en: a tidal woodland of mangrove trees growing along tropical and subtropical shores
core_image: 一片密不透风的绿色树冠架在无数支柱根上，潮水在根间穿行
scene: 潮水漫进林下，密集的树冠把正午的光切成碎片，支柱根在浑水里交错。 The mangrove forest shelters young fish among its tangled roots.
sceneCN: 这里指「由红树构成的潮间带林地」（第 1 个义项：热带或亚热带海岸上成片生长、受潮汐淹没的红树林）；句意为红树林在盘错的根系间庇护幼鱼。场景物件：树冠、支柱根、浑水、幼鱼。

pos.zh: 红树林；红树林森林（可数；复数 mangrove forests）

collocations.phrase: the canopy of a mangrove forest

forms.label: 生态学术语（红树林群落）

senses.title: A tidal woodland of mangroves
senses.definition: a tidal woodland of mangrove trees growing along tropical and subtropical shores
senses.definitionCN: 热带与亚热带海岸上成片生长、受潮汐作用的红树构成的林地
senses.example: The mangrove forest shelters young fish among its tangled roots.
senses.exampleCN: 红树林在盘错的根系间庇护幼鱼。
senses.why: Mangrove names the tree and forest names the woodland, so the compound names the stand as a vegetation type rather than a single plant.
senses.whyCN: mangrove 指树，forest 指林地，因此复合词命名的是一片植被类型，而不是单株。

senses.title: A tropical intertidal forest
senses.definition: the forest formation found where tropical shores are flooded by tides
senses.definitionCN: 热带海岸受潮汐淹没处形成的森林类型
senses.example: Mangrove forest replaces salt marsh where frost is absent.
senses.exampleCN: 在没有霜冻的地方，红树林取代了盐沼。
senses.why: In global vegetation mapping the term marks a climatic zone as much as a plant, so it names a formation.
senses.whyCN: 在全球植被制图中，这个术语既标记气候带也标记植物，因此它命名一种植被型。

senses.title: Canopy and root architecture
senses.definition: the layered canopy, stilt roots and breathing roots that give the forest its physical structure
senses.definitionCN: 层叠的林冠、支柱根与呼吸根所构成的森林物理结构
senses.example: The mangrove forest has a canopy closed enough to shade the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 红树林的林冠密到能遮住泥面。
senses.why: Foresters describe a stand by its layers and roots, so the phrase can name the architecture rather than the species list.
senses.whyCN: 林业人员按层次与根系描述林分，因此这个短语也能指结构本身，而非物种清单。

senses.title: A functioning ecosystem
senses.definition: the community of trees, animals, microbes and sediment that functions as one system
senses.definitionCN: 树木、动物、微生物与沉积物共同作为一个系统运作的群落
senses.example: The mangrove forest recycles nutrients within its own mud.
senses.exampleCN: 红树林在自己的泥里循环养分。
senses.why: When the focus moves from trees to flows of energy and matter, the woodland becomes an ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 当重点从树转向能量与物质的流动，林地就变成了生态系统。

senses.title: A blue-carbon accounting unit
senses.definition: the forest and its sediment counted together as a carbon stock
senses.definitionCN: 把森林与其沉积物合起来计算的碳储量
senses.example: The mangrove forest stores more carbon per hectare than the inland wood.
senses.exampleCN: 每公顷红树林储存的碳多于内陆林地。
senses.why: Carbon markets need a boundary, so the stand plus its mud became one accounting unit.
senses.whyCN: 碳市场需要边界，于是林分连同泥层成了一个核算单元。

senses.title: A coastal defence belt
senses.definition: the belt of trees and roots that reduces wave height and storm surge
senses.definitionCN: 降低波高与风暴潮的树木与根系带
senses.example: The mangrove forest broke the surge before it reached the seawall.
senses.exampleCN: 红树林在风暴潮抵达海堤前把它打散。
senses.why: Coastal engineers measured the forest as a barrier, so the stand acquired a defence function.
senses.whyCN: 海岸工程师把这片林当作屏障来测量，林分于是获得防护功能。

senses.title: A nursery ground
senses.definition: the sheltered root maze where juvenile fish and crustaceans grow
senses.definitionCN: 幼鱼与甲壳类在根系迷宫中生长的庇护所
senses.example: Shrimp leave the mangrove forest only when they are almost adult.
senses.exampleCN: 虾几乎成年时才离开红树林。
senses.why: Fisheries science found that the forest is a nursery, so the place name became a function name.
senses.whyCN: 渔业科学发现这片林是育幼场，地名于是变成功能名。

senses.title: A restoration and policy unit
senses.definition: a mapped forest area used in restoration targets, reserves and offsets
senses.definitionCN: 用于修复目标、保护区与补偿项目的图定林地
senses.example: The province pledged to restore a thousand hectares of mangrove forest.
senses.exampleCN: 该省承诺修复一千公顷红树林。
senses.why: Policy needs hectares and boundaries, so the vegetation type became a unit of planning.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要公顷与边界，于是植被类型成了规划单元。

intro.en: Mangrove forest joins a borrowed tropical tree name of disputed origin to forest, a word from medieval Latin forestis 'outside place'. The compound is modern ecology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mangrove forest 把一个来源有争议的借入树名与 forest 组合起来，后者出自中世纪拉丁 forestis「外围之地」。这个复合词属现代生态学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mangrove came to English through Portuguese or Spanish trade forms; Tupi, Malay and English grove have all been proposed as influences, and none is proven.
items.cn: mangrove 经葡萄牙语或西班牙语贸易词形进入英语；图皮语、马来语与英语 grove 都被提出过影响，但都未获证明。

items.en: Forestis meant 'outside place' or 'wooded land outside the settlement'; it gave Old French forest and English forest.
items.cn: forestis 意为「外围之地」或「聚落之外的林地」，形成古法语 forest 与英语 forest。

items.en: The compound pairs a borrowed tropical name with a native-feeling but ultimately Latin-derived word, a common pattern in scientific English.
items.cn: 这个复合词把一个借入的热带名称与一个感觉像本族词、实则源自拉丁的 forest 配在一起，这是科技术语的常见模式。

items.en: Travelers and colonial surveyors wrote of mangrove forests before ecologists had a formal category for them.
items.cn: 在生态学家建立正式类别之前，旅行者与殖民地测量员已在使用红树林这一说法。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology fixed the phrase as the name of a tropical intertidal formation, distinct from salt marsh and swamp forest.
items.cn: 二十世纪生态学把这个短语定为热带潮间带植被型的名称，与盐沼及沼泽林区分。

items.en: Source uncertain (word origin and first date): the origin of mangrove remains disputed, and the first printed use of the full compound is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词源与首见年代）：mangrove 的来源仍有争议，完整复合词最早的印刷记录没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the tree, stand and ecological names that overlap; group two holds other wooded or tidal systems often mistaken for this forest.
note.cn: 第一组是相互重叠的树、林分与生态名称；第二组是常被误认作红树林的其他林地或潮汐系统。

entries.definition: A single tree or the plant kind; mangrove forest is the woodland made of many such trees.
entries.definitionCN: 单株树或这一类植物；mangrove forest 是由许多这样的树构成的林地。

entries.definition: The ecological community of mangroves; it overlaps with the forest but stresses the living assemblage rather than the woodland.
entries.definitionCN: 红树的生态群落；它与红树林重叠，但强调活的组合而不是林地本身。

entries.definition: The waterlogged ground under the trees; the forest names the trees, the swamp names the wet substrate.
entries.definitionCN: 树下的饱水地面；森林指树，沼泽指湿基底。

entries.definition: Any large wooded area; mangrove forest restricts the woodland to tidal salt water and tropical shores.
entries.definitionCN: 任何大片林地；mangrove forest 把林地限定到潮汐咸水与热带海岸。

entries.definition: A tidal meadow of salt-tolerant grasses; it occupies a similar zone but has no tree canopy.
entries.definitionCN: 耐盐禾草组成的潮汐草甸；它占据相似地带，却没有树冠。

entries.definition: A forest on waterlogged freshwater ground; it is flooded but not tidal and not salty.
entries.definitionCN: 建在饱水淡水地面上的森林；它被水淹，但不受潮汐作用，也不咸。

entries.definition: Any wetland shaped by tides; mangrove forest is one woody member of this wider class.
entries.definitionCN: 任何受潮汐塑造的湿地；红树林是这一更宽类别中的木本成员。

entries.definition: Woodland near the coast but above the tide; it lacks salt flooding and aerial roots.
entries.definitionCN: 靠近海岸但位于潮线以上的林地；它没有咸水淹浸与气生根。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real ecological categories and real conservation collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实复合词、真实生态类别与真实保护搭配。

normal.en: Mangrove names the tree; forest names the woodland.
normal.cn: mangrove 指树；forest 指林地。

normal.en: The forest forms where tropical shores are flooded by tides.
normal.cn: 这片林形成于受潮汐淹没的热带海岸。

normal.en: Its canopy, stilt roots and breathing roots are its architecture.
normal.cn: 林冠、支柱根与呼吸根是它的建筑结构。

normal.en: Mangrove forest is a nursery, a carbon store and a storm barrier.
normal.cn: 红树林是育幼场、碳库与风暴屏障。

normal.en: Restoration targets are counted in hectares of mangrove forest.
normal.cn: 修复目标按红树林公顷数计算。

abstract.en: Picture a green roof held above the water by thousands of wooden legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿色屋顶，被成千上万条木腿撑在水面之上。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the streets are roots and the citizens are fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城，街道是根，居民是鱼。

abstract.en: Picture a forest that files carbon into the mud like documents into a vault.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林，把碳像档案一样存进泥的保险库。

examples.en: The mangrove forest was cleared for shrimp ponds.
examples.cn: 红树林被清掉，改成了养虾池。

examples.en: A healthy mangrove forest can raise the shore as sea level rises.
examples.cn: 健康的红树林能在海面上升时把岸面抬高。

examples.en: The map shows mangrove forest retreating along the delta.
examples.cn: 地图显示红树林沿三角洲后退。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mangrove（红树）+ forest（森林）」——红树构成的潮间带森林 → 红树林

root: mangrove 来源有争议：或出自葡萄牙语 mangue（可能来自图皮语），或与马来语 manggi-manggi 有关，另有英语 grove 影响词形的推测；forest 出自中世纪拉丁 forestis「外围之地」→ 古法语 forest。复合词为现代生态学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one woodland: a vegetation type, a tropical formation, a canopy architecture, an ecosystem, a carbon unit, a defence belt, a nursery and a policy unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一片林地展开：植被类型、热带植被型、林冠结构、生态系统、碳单元、防护带、育幼场与政策单元。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense green canopy held above muddy tidal water by countless stilt roots.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片浓密绿冠由无数支柱根撑在浑黄的潮水之上。

branches.en: TREE TO FORMATION: a stand of one kind of tree becomes a mapped vegetation type across a climate zone.
branches.cn: 从树到植被型：一片同种树林变成跨越气候带的图定植被类型。

branches.en: STRUCTURE MAKES FUNCTION: canopy and roots create the shade, shelter and sediment traps that the ecosystem runs on.
branches.cn: 结构产生功能：林冠与根系造出荫蔽、庇护与截沙，生态系统靠此运转。

branches.en: THE CARBON STOCK: the wet, slow-decay system is measured as stored carbon.
branches.cn: 碳储量：这套湿而慢分解的系统被计为储碳。

branches.en: THE BREAKWATER: the stand takes energy out of waves before they reach the shore.
branches.cn: 防波带：实体林分在波浪抵达岸前抽走能量。

branches.en: NURSERY TO POLICY: a function valued by fisheries becomes a hectare target in restoration policy.
branches.cn: 从育幼到政策：渔业看重的功能变成修复政策中的公顷目标。

intro.en: Mangrove forest is a compound of a borrowed tree name and a Latin-derived woodland word; both parts are free morphemes, and the phrase is best read as a label for a formation.
intro.cn: mangrove forest 是一个由借入树名与拉丁来源林地词构成的复合词；两部分都是自由语素，最好把它读作一种植被型的标签。

latinIntro.en: Only forest has a Latin line, through medieval forestis; mangrove has no established Latin ancestor, so the Latin layer is partial.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 forest 有拉丁线索，经由中世纪 forestis；mangrove 没有已确立的拉丁祖先，因此拉丁层只是部分的。

items.example: The medieval term marked land beyond the village.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪词标记村庄之外的土地。

items.example: Forestry maps the stand by canopy height.
items.exampleCN: 林业按林冠高度绘制林分。

items.example: The mangrove forest floods twice a day.

items.exampleCN: 保护之后红树林丧失减慢。

items.example: The canopy closes over the creek.
The mangal is rich in molluscs.
items.exampleCN: 红树群落软体动物丰富。

latinEntries.meaning: outside; wooded land outside a settlement
latinEntries.meaningCN: 外围的；聚落之外的林地

latinEntries.structure: canopeum, canopeī (n., second declension; from Greek)
latinEntries.meaning: a mosquito net; later a canopy

definition_zh: 回归；倒退；（统计学）回归分析、回归模型；（疾病）消退；（海平面下降造成的）海退
definition_en: a return to an earlier or worse state, or the statistical method that estimates how variables are related to an outcome
core_image: 散点图上一条线穿过云一样的点，最偏的点被慢慢拉回中间
scene: 实验室里，学生把两年的成绩画成散点图，想看出每天多学一小时能带来多少分。 The team used a regression to see how study hours predicted exam scores.
sceneCN: 这里 regression 指「用数据估计变量之间关系的统计方法」（第 2 个义项：回归分析）；句意：研究小组用一次回归分析看学习时长如何预测考试分数。图中可辨识物件：散点图、拟合直线、坐标轴、记录表。

pos.zh: 回归；倒退；回归分析；消退

senses.title: A step back to a former state
senses.definition: a movement back to an earlier condition, especially one that is worse or less advanced
senses.definitionCN: 退回从前的状况，尤指退到更差或更落后的状态
senses.example: The village saw a regression into old habits after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，这个村子又退回了旧习惯。
senses.why: Regressio is literally a stepping back, so the word names any movement that reverses an advance.
senses.whyCN: regressio 本义是往回走一步，因此可指任何让进展倒退的变化。

senses.title: The statistical method of fitting a relation
senses.titleCN: 拟合变量关系的统计方法
senses.definition: the statistical technique that estimates how one or more input variables are related to an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 估计一个或多个输入变量与结果之间关系的统计方法
senses.example: The team ran a regression to test whether study hours predicted scores.
senses.exampleCN: 研究小组做了一次回归分析，检验学习时长能否预测分数。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century work on inherited traits gave this name to a method that measures how one variable moves with another.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪研究遗传特征的工作，把测量一个变量随另一个变量变化的方法定名为回归。

senses.title: The fitted line itself
senses.definition: the line or curve drawn through a cloud of data points to summarise the estimated relationship
senses.definitionCN: 穿过一堆数据点、用来概括估计关系的直线或曲线
senses.example: Each extra hour raised the regression line by four points.
senses.exampleCN: 每多学一小时，回归线上移四分。
senses.why: Once a relation is estimated it is drawn, and the drawing borrows the name of the method that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 关系一旦被估计出来就要画成线，这条线便沿用了产生它的方法之名。

senses.title: Extremes drifting back toward the average
senses.definition: the tendency of unusually high or low measurements to move closer to the average when measured again
senses.definitionCN: 异常偏高或偏低的测量值在再次测量时向平均值靠拢的倾向
senses.example: The second test showed regression to the mean among the top scorers.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次测验中，高分者出现了向平均值回归的现象。
senses.why: An extreme score contains more luck than usual, so a repeat measurement tends to drift back toward the centre.
senses.whyCN: 极端分数里包含比平常更多的运气成分，再测一次就容易向中间漂。

senses.title: A family of extended models
senses.definition: one of the model variants that add several predictors or handle a categorical outcome
senses.definitionCN: 增加多个预测变量、或处理分类结果的一类模型变体
senses.example: Logistic regression suits a yes-or-no outcome better than a straight line.
senses.exampleCN: 结果只有是或否时，逻辑回归比一条直线更合适。
senses.why: The same fitting idea branches into variants when the inputs multiply or the outcome becomes a category.
senses.whyCN: 当输入变量增多或结果变成类别，同一套拟合思路就分出多种变体。

senses.title: A disease or tumour retreating
senses.definition: the shrinking or retreat of a disease, growth or tumour under treatment
senses.definitionCN: 疾病、增生物或肿瘤在治疗下缩小、退去
senses.example: The scan showed regression of the tumour after six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 六周后的扫描显示肿瘤已经消退。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word for a disease that steps back from the body it had invaded.
senses.whyCN: 医学借这个词表示疾病从它侵占的身体部位退回去。

senses.title: A child losing learned skills
senses.titleCN: 儿童失去已学会的技能
senses.definition: the loss of skills a child had already acquired, such as speech, play or toilet use
senses.definitionCN: 儿童失去已经掌握的技能，如说话、玩耍或如厕
senses.example: The parents reported a regression in their son's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 父母说儿子的语言能力出现了倒退。
senses.why: A child who loses ground is stepping backward along the developmental path, which is the oldest image of the word.
senses.whyCN: 孩子失去已有的进展，就是沿发育路径往回走，正是这个词最古老的意象。

senses.title: The sea withdrawing from the land
senses.definition: the retreat of the shoreline, usually caused by falling sea level or rising land
senses.definitionCN: 海岸线后退，通常由海平面下降或陆地抬升引起
senses.example: The sandstone records a regression of the sea in the Jurassic.
senses.exampleCN: 这片砂岩记录了侏罗纪的一次海退。
senses.why: Geology treats the shoreline as a line that can step back, reusing the same image as the general sense.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把海岸线看成一条可以后退的线，沿用了一般义项里的同一意象。

intro.en: Regression comes from Latin regressio 'a going back', a noun of action from regredi 'to step back', built on re- 'back' plus gradi 'to step'. English took the word through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: regression 出自拉丁 regressio「退回」，是 regredi「往回走」的名词形式，由 re-「向后」加 gradi「走」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gradus meant 'step, pace', and it also gives English grade, gradual and graduate; the step is the physical core of the family.
items.cn: gradus 意为「步、步伐」，也衍生出英语 grade、gradual 与 graduate；「步」是这一族词的实体核心。

items.en: Gradi was a deponent verb 'to step, go', built on the same stem; progress, regress and retrograde all combine a direction prefix with this verb.
items.cn: gradi 是异态动词「迈步、走」，词干相同；progress、regress 与 retrograde 都是方向前缀加这个动词。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus gradi produced regredi 'to step back, return', which describes a physical withdrawal before it describes a statistical one.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 gradi 构成 regredi「往回走、返回」，先描述身体后退，后才用于统计。

items.en: Regressio was the noun of action, 'a going back'; it entered English through French as a general word for a return or a backward movement.
items.cn: regressio 是动作名词「退回」，经法语进入英语，最初泛指返回或后退。

items.en: Francis Galton used the term in the 1880s for the tendency of extreme inherited traits to move toward the average, and regression later became the name of the fitting method itself.
items.cn: 高尔顿在一八八〇年代用这个词描述极端遗传特征向平均值靠拢的倾向，后来 regression 又成为整套拟合方法的名称。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin regressio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The pre-Latin origin of gradus is reconstructed rather than attested, and the reconstruction is offered as a form, not as a demonstrated word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 regressio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的确切年代没有记录。gradus 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式而非有据可查，该形式只是重构，并非已证实的词。

note.en: Group one follows the gradi stock, where a direction prefix decides whether a step goes forward, backward or sideways; group two holds ordinary words for going back to a previous state.
note.cn: 第一组同出 gradi 词干，方向前缀决定这一步是向前、向后还是绕行；第二组是表达回到从前状态的普通词。

entries.definition: To go back to an earlier or worse state; the verb without the statistical noun ending.
entries.definitionCN: 回到更早或更差的状态；是不带统计名词后缀的动词形式。

entries.definition: Pro- 'forward' plus gradi: a step in the other direction, so the two words are mirror images.
entries.definitionCN: pro-「向前」加 gradi：朝相反方向迈步，两词正好互为镜像。

entries.definition: Retro- 'backward' plus gradi: moving backward, used of planets, steps or policies.
entries.definitionCN: retro-「向后」加 gradi：向后移动，用于行星、步骤或政策。

entries.definition: From gradus 'step': happening one step at a time, with no statistical sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 gradus「步」：一步一步发生，完全不含统计义。

entries.definition: The plain word for coming back to a place or state, carrying no judgement about whether it is worse.
entries.definitionCN: 回到某地或某状态的普通说法，不判断变好还是变坏。

entries.definition: A return of illness after improvement, close to the medical sense of regression but used of patients rather than scans.
entries.definitionCN: 病情好转后又复发，接近 regression 的医学义，但多用于病人而非影像。

entries.definition: A going back to an earlier form or type, often in biology, without the fitted-line sense.
entries.definitionCN: 回到早先形态或类型，常用于生物学，不含拟合线之义。

entries.definition: A fall in quality or amount; it stresses loss rather than the act of stepping back.
entries.definitionCN: 质量或数量下降；强调损失，而非往回走这个动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin step, the statistical line and the real medical and geological uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「步」、统计里的那条线，以及真实的医学与地质用法。

normal.en: Re- 'back' plus gradi 'to step': one step backward.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 gradi「走」：往回迈一步。

normal.en: The same family gives progress, retrograde and gradual.
normal.cn: 同族词给出 progress、retrograde 与 gradual。

normal.en: In statistics the line makes extreme points drift back to the middle.
normal.cn: 统计里那条线让偏远的点漂回中间。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: linear regression, regression analysis, regression to the mean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：线性回归、回归分析、向平均值回归。

normal.en: Medicine says a tumour regresses when it shrinks.
normal.cn: 医学说肿瘤消退时也用这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hiker who turns around one step before the summit.
abstract.cn: 想象登山者在离山顶一步时转身往回走。

abstract.en: Picture a graph line quietly pulling the furthest dots inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条图线把最远的点悄悄拉回内侧。

abstract.en: Picture a shoreline moving away from the houses it once reached.
abstract.cn: 想象海岸线从它曾抵达的房屋前退开。

examples.en: A single regression cannot prove causation, only a measured association.
examples.cn: 一次回归分析不能证明因果，只能给出测得的关联。

examples.en: The report described a regression in reading skills among younger pupils.
examples.cn: 报告描述了低年级学生阅读能力的倒退。

examples.en: Geologists read the rock layer as evidence of a marine regression.
examples.cn: 地质学家把这一岩层读作海退的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ gress（走）」——往回走：回归、倒退；统计里让点回到线附近

root: 拉丁 regressio「退回」= regredi（re-「向后」+ gradi「走」）的名词形式；gradi 出自 gradus「步」。同根词有 progress、retrograde、gradual。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one backward step: a return to a worse state, a measured relation, the line that draws it, extremes drifting inward, a family of models, a tumour retreating, a child losing skills and a shoreline withdrawing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「往回走」：退回更差的状态、被测量的关系、画出关系的线、极端值向内漂、扩展出的模型家族、肿瘤消退、孩子失去技能，以及海岸线后退。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one step taken backward, away from where the path had reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝后迈出一步，离开原本已经走到的地方。

branches.en: GOING BACK: a village losing its habits and a tumour shrinking are the same backward step at different scales.
branches.cn: 往回走：村子丢掉新习惯与肿瘤缩小，是同一后退动作在不同尺度上的样子。

branches.en: MEASURE THEN DRAW: the method estimates a relation and the line makes that estimate visible.
branches.cn: 先测量再画线：方法估计出关系，线把估计结果画出来。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE PULLS: extreme scores contain luck, so a repeat drifts toward the average.
branches.cn: 中间有拉力：极端分数含运气，重测就向平均值漂。

branches.en: THE FAMILY GROWS: more predictors and categorical outcomes split one fitting idea into variants.
branches.cn: 家族扩张：更多预测变量与分类结果，把一套拟合思路分成多种变体。

branches.en: SMALL AND LARGE RETREATS: a child losing speech and a sea leaving the land both move backward from a reached line.
branches.cn: 小尺度与大尺度的退却：孩子失去语言与海水离开陆地，都是从已抵达的界线后退。

intro.en: Regression is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun ending, and every piece also builds other English words.
intro.cn: regression 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词根与名词词尾构成，每一部分也都参与构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Re- 'back' combines with gradi 'to step'; gradus 'step' supplies grade, gradual and graduate, while -io forms action nouns such as regressio.
latinIntro.cn: re-「向后」与 gradi「走」组合；gradus「步」衍生 grade、gradual 与 graduate，-io 则构成 regressio 这类动作名词。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of the step.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把步伐的方向反过来。

items.example: Grade and gradual both descend from this noun.
items.exampleCN: grade 与 gradual 都出自这个名词。

items.example: Every direction prefix needs this verb to make a motion word.
items.exampleCN: 每个方向前缀都要配这个动词才能造出运动词。

items.example: The verb describes the body before it describes data.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词先描述身体，再用于数据。

items.example: The Latin noun became the English word through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词经法语变成英语词。

items.example: The policy was criticised as regressive.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策被批评为倒退。

items.example: Progress is the mirror image of regress.
items.exampleCN: progress 正是 regress 的镜像。

items.example: The planet appears retrograde from Earth.
items.exampleCN: 从地球看这颗行星像在逆行。

items.example: The change was gradual rather than sudden.
items.exampleCN: 变化是逐步的，不是突然的。

definition_zh: v. 为（他人或自己所受的伤害）报仇；替……复仇
definition_en: To inflict punishment in return for a wrong done to oneself or to another person.
core_image: 替倒下的人把那一击还回去
scene: 他发誓要替被害的兄弟报仇。 He swore to avenge his murdered brother.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：avenge 指为他人所受的伤害而施加惩罚，宾语通常是受害者或那桩伤害。

senses.title: Punish a wrong for someone
senses.titleCN: 替他人所受的伤害施加惩罚
senses.definition: to take or exact punishment for a harm suffered by another person or by oneself
senses.definitionCN: 为他人或自己所受的伤害而施加或索取惩罚
senses.example: They raised an army to avenge the raid.
senses.exampleCN: 他们集结军队为那次袭击复仇。
senses.why: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Latin vindicare, to claim or punish, so it directs a claim of justice at a wrong.
senses.whyCN: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，因此它把一份正义诉求指向那桩伤害。

senses.title: Reflexive retaliation
senses.definition: in a reflexive pattern with on, to pay back a personal injury by harming the offender
senses.definitionCN: 用于带 on 的反身句式，指以伤害冒犯者来回报自身所受的损害
senses.example: He avenged himself on the men who cheated him.
senses.exampleCN: 他向那些骗过他的人复仇。
senses.why: The reflexive keeps the injured party in view, which is what separates avenge from revenge in careful use.
senses.whyCN: 反身式让受害者始终在视野之中，这正是严谨用法中 avenge 与 revenge 的分界。

intro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge, from Old French avengier, from Latin vindicare, to lay claim to or punish, from vindex, a claimant or avenger.
intro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，出自古法语 avengier，源自拉丁语 vindicare「索还、惩罚」，而 vindicare 出自 vindex「索求者、复仇者」。

items.en: A root meaning to point out or claim stands behind words of showing and demanding.
items.cn: 一个表示「指出、索求」的词根支撑着显示与要求类的词。

items.en: Latin vindex named a claimant, one who demands a thing back or answers for a wrong.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vindex 指索求者，即索回某物或为不公讨回公道的人。

items.en: From it vindicare meant to lay claim to, to set free, and to punish.
items.cn: 由此 vindicare 意为「索还、释放、惩罚」。

items.en: Old French venger kept the punishing side, to take vengeance for a harm.
items.cn: 古法语 venger 保留了惩罚一面，即为伤害复仇。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave avengier, to direct that punishment at a wrong.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 avengier，即把惩罚指向某桩伤害。

items.en: Middle English avengen entered in the fourteenth century and displaced older native words.
items.cn: 中古英语 avengen 于十四世纪进入，取代了更早的本族词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the venge family; the near-meaning group lists other words for paying back a wrong.
note.cn: 形近组保留 venge 词族；近义组列出其他表示回报伤害的词。

normalIntro.en: Avenge is a- plus venge, kin to vengeance: aim the payback at a wrong done to someone.
normalIntro.cn: avenge 是 a- 加 venge，与 vengeance 同族：把回报瞄准某人所受的伤害。

normal.en: Avenge takes the victim or the wrong as object.

normal.en: Vindicate shares the root but means to clear.

definition_zh: n. 女校友；女毕业生（复数 alumnae）
definition_en: A female former student or graduate of a school, college or university; the plural form is alumnae.
core_image: 毕业多年后仍被母校叫作「养女」的那个人
scene: 她毕业二十年，每年校庆都坐在第一排。 The college honoured its oldest alumna at the ceremony.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：她是从这所学院毕业的女性，所以用 alumna 而不是 alumnus。校方在校庆上向这位最年长的女校友致敬。

senses.title: A female graduate
senses.definition: a woman who formerly studied at a particular school, college or university
senses.definitionCN: 曾在某所学校、学院或大学就读的女性
senses.example: She is an alumna of the medical school.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这所医学院的女校友。
senses.why: Latin alumnus meant a foster child or pupil, one nourished by a household; the -a ending marks the feminine, so the school is still pictured as a foster mother.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alumnus 意为养子或学生，即被一个家庭养育的人；-a 词尾标示阴性，因此学校仍被想象为养母。

senses.title: In institutional records
senses.definition: used by colleges in titles, lists and fundraising to identify women on the graduate roll
senses.definitionCN: 高校在头衔、名录与募捐中用以标识毕业生名册上的女性
senses.example: The alumnae fund paid for two new scholarships.
senses.exampleCN: 女校友基金资助了两项新奖学金。
senses.why: Institutions keep the Latin plurals because their rolls are formal documents, so alumnae appears where speech would simply say alums.
senses.whyCN: 院校保留拉丁语复数，因为名录属于正式文件，所以在口语只说 alums 的地方，书面仍写 alumnae。

intro.en: Alumna is the feminine of Latin alumnus, a foster child or pupil, from alere, to nourish. The school is imagined as the household that fed you, and the ending tells the gender.
intro.cn: alumna 是拉丁语 alumnus 的阴性形式，alumnus 意为养子或学生，来自 alere「滋养」。学校被想象为喂养过你的那个家，词尾则标示性别。

items.en: Latin alere meant to nourish, feed or bring up. The same root gives aliment, alimentary and, through altus, altitude.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alere 意为「滋养、喂养、养育」。同一词根产生 aliment、alimentary，并经 altus 产生 altitude。

items.en: Alumnus was the noun for a foster son or pupil, literally one who is nourished. A teacher or a school stood in the place of a parent.
items.cn: alumnus 是表示养子或学生的名词，字面为「被养育的人」。老师或学校站在父母的位置上。

items.en: Alumna is the feminine singular and alumnae the feminine plural, while alumnus and alumni are the masculine pair. English borrowed all four intact.
items.cn: alumna 是阴性单数，alumnae 是阴性复数，而 alumnus 与 alumni 是阳性的一对。英语把四个形式整套借入。

items.en: English took alumnus in the seventeenth century and alumna later, as women began to keep their own graduate rolls at colleges.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 alumnus，alumna 较晚，随着女性开始在高校拥有自己的毕业生名册而通行。

items.en: Today alum serves for any gender in speech, while formal writing still separates alumna, alumnae, alumnus and alumni.
items.cn: 如今口语中 alum 不分性别通用，而正式书面语仍区分 alumna、alumnae、alumnus 与 alumni。

note.en: The look-alike group lines up the four Latin forms and the near spelling album; the near-meaning group lists other words for a former student.
note.cn: 形近组排列四个拉丁语形式与拼写相近的 album；近义组列出其他表示「 former student 」的说法。

abstract.en: Think of a name list where the ending tells you who is who.

examples.en: The alumnae gathered in the old library.

examples.en: She is a proud alumna of a small state college.
examples.cn: 她是一所小型州立学院的自豪校友。

definition_zh: 气团；气团源地；冷气团；暖气团；气团变性
definition_en: a large body of air with broadly uniform temperature and humidity, shaped over a source region and later modified as it moves
core_image: 一整块温湿度均匀的空气像看不见的厚毯盖住大陆，边缘与另一块空气相撞处云带陡起
scene: 北方的干冷空气整块南下，盆地的气温一夜之间降了下来。 A cold air mass moved south and chilled the whole basin.
sceneCN: 这里指「性质水平均匀的大块空气」（第 1 个义项：在源地获得温湿度特征的大范围气块）；句意为一个冷气团南下，使整个盆地变冷。图中可辨识物件：整块推进的冷空气、被压低的云带、结霜的田面、下降的温度计。

pos.zh: 气团；气团源地；冷气团；暖气团

senses.title: A large body of uniform air
senses.titleCN: 性质水平均匀的大块空气
senses.definition: a large volume of air whose temperature and humidity vary little across hundreds of kilometres
senses.definitionCN: 在数百公里范围内温度与湿度变化很小的大体积空气
senses.example: A cold air mass moved south and chilled the whole basin.
senses.exampleCN: 一个冷气团南下，使整个盆地变冷。
senses.why: Meteorology needed a unit larger than a local parcel and more uniform than the whole atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 气象学需要一个比局地气块更大、又比整个大气更均匀的单位。

senses.title: The source region where it forms
senses.definition: the extensive surface, ocean or ice, over which an air mass acquires its temperature and moisture
senses.definitionCN: 气团借以获得温度与湿度的大面积地表、海洋或冰面
senses.example: The polar air mass formed over the ice and kept its low humidity.
senses.exampleCN: 极地气团在冰面上形成，并保持了低湿度。
senses.why: A body of air takes the character of the ground it sits on, so the ground gets a name too.
senses.whyCN: 空气会带上它所停留地面的性格，因此地面也有了一个名称。

senses.title: Classification by latitude and surface
senses.definition: the grouping of air masses as polar or tropical and as continental or maritime
senses.definitionCN: 按极地或热带、大陆或海洋来划分气团
senses.example: Forecasters labelled the air mass continental polar.
senses.exampleCN: 预报员把该气团标为大陆极地气团。
senses.why: Two axes, latitude and surface, give four main types, which is enough for synoptic charts.
senses.whyCN: 纬度与下垫面两条轴给出四种主要类型，对天气图分析已经够用。

senses.title: A cold air mass
senses.definition: an air mass colder than the surface beneath it, which cools the ground as it passes
senses.definitionCN: 比所经地面更冷、经过时使地面降温的气团
senses.example: A cold air mass brought frost to the vineyards.
senses.exampleCN: 冷气团给葡萄园带来了霜。
senses.why: The label is relative: the same air is 'cold' only with respect to what lies under it.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签是相对的：同一团空气只是相对于其下方的表面才称为冷。

senses.title: A warm air mass
senses.definition: an air mass warmer than the surface beneath it, which warms the ground as it passes
senses.definitionCN: 比所经地面更暖、经过时使地面升温的气团
senses.example: A warm air mass from the sea raised the night temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 来自海上的暖气团抬高了夜间气温。
senses.why: The warm label follows the same relative logic as the cold one.
senses.whyCN: 暖气团的标签遵循与冷气团相同的相对逻辑。

senses.title: Modification as it travels
senses.titleCN: 移动过程中的气团变性
senses.definition: the change an air mass undergoes when it passes over a surface with different temperature or moisture
senses.definitionCN: 气团经过温度或湿度不同的下垫面时发生的变化
senses.example: Air-mass modification turned the dry continental air into a snow producer.
senses.exampleCN: 气团变性把干燥的大陆空气变成了能下雪的气团。
senses.why: Air is not sealed; it exchanges heat and water with every surface it crosses.
senses.whyCN: 空气不是密封的；它每经过一个表面都会交换热量与水汽。

senses.title: The boundary between two air masses
senses.definition: the sloping surface where two air masses meet, which is what a front maps
senses.definitionCN: 两个气团相遇的倾斜界面，锋面所描绘的正是这个界面
senses.example: Where the two air masses met, a front sharpened the rain into a line.
senses.exampleCN: 两个气团相遇之处，锋面把降雨收束成一条线。
senses.why: A front is not a separate object but the visible consequence of two air masses touching.
senses.whyCN: 锋面不是独立物体，而是两个气团接触后可见的结果。

senses.title: A homogeneous bloc, figuratively
senses.definition: a large, uniform group or mood that moves as a single body through a population
senses.definitionCN: 在人群中作为整体移动的一大块同质群体或情绪
senses.example: An air mass of indifference settled over the electorate.
senses.exampleCN: 一大团冷漠笼罩了选民。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps size and internal uniformity, not the weather.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留体量与内部同质性，而不保留天气。

intro.en: Air mass joins air, from Greek aēr through Latin aer, and mass, from Latin massa 'lump', itself from Greek maza. The meteorological compound was coined in the early twentieth century by the Norwegian school of forecasting.
intro.cn: air mass 由 air 与 mass 组合。air 经拉丁 aer 出自希腊 aēr；mass 出自拉丁 massa「团块」，其源又是希腊 maza。这个气象复合词由挪威预报学派在 20 世纪初造出。

items.en: Greek aēr named the lower, misty air; Latin aer carried it into learned European vocabulary.
items.cn: 希腊 aēr 指低层有雾的空气；拉丁 aer 把它带入欧洲学术词汇。

items.en: Massa meant a lump or mass, from Greek maza 'kneaded dough', and gave English mass in both physical and figurative senses.
items.cn: massa 指团块，源自希腊 maza「揉好的面团」，并给出英语 mass 的物理义与比喻义。

items.en: Forecasters at Bergen in the early twentieth century treated the atmosphere as colliding bodies of air and named those bodies air masses.
items.cn: 20 世纪初卑尔根的预报员把大气视为相互碰撞的空气体，并把这些空气体命名为气团。

items.en: The same school classified air masses by source latitude and surface, and linked their boundaries to fronts.
items.cn: 同一学派按源地纬度与下垫面对气团分类，并把它们的交界与锋面联系起来。

items.en: Later work on air-mass modification explained how cold continental air becomes unstable over warm sea.
items.cn: 后来的气团变性研究解释了冷大陆空气经过暖海面时如何变得不稳定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact year the compound entered print is reported differently, and the priority between Bergen authors is debated; the technical meaning itself is settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：复合词进入印刷的确切年份各家记述不同，卑尔根诸作者的首创权亦有争议；技术含义本身已确定。

note.en: Group one holds terms built on the same two words or on the same concept; group two holds neighbouring atmospheric bodies and boundaries.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个词或同一概念构成的术语；第二组是邻近的大气气块与交界名称。

entries.definition: The same term written as one word, common in meteorology texts; there is no difference in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的连写形式，常见于气象文献；含义没有差别。

entries.definition: A thunderstorm formed within one air mass rather than at a front; the phrase is not the air mass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一气团内部而非锋面处形成的雷暴；该短语并非气团本身。

entries.definition: A quantity of matter or a large body of anything; only the meteorological compound adds 'uniform air'.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的数量，或任何事物的一大团；只有气象复合词才增加「均匀空气」这层意思。

entries.definition: A small imagined volume used in thermodynamics; an air mass is millions of such parcels sharing properties.
entries.definitionCN: 热力学中使用的小体积想象单位；气团是共享性质的大量此类气块。

entries.definition: The sloping interface between two air masses; the air masses are the bodies, the front is their contact.
entries.definitionCN: 两个气团之间的倾斜界面；气团是体，锋面是它们的接触处。

entries.definition: Any organised atmospheric structure, including lows, highs and air masses; it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有组织的大气结构，包括低压、高压与气团；并非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek and Latin sources and the real Bergen-school origin.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁来源，以及真实的卑尔根学派源头。

normal.en: Air plus mass: a lump of air big enough to cover a region.
normal.cn: air 加 mass：一大团大到能覆盖一个区域的空气。

normal.en: Two axes classify it: polar or tropical, continental or maritime.
normal.cn: 两条轴给气团分类：极地或热带、大陆或海洋。

normal.en: The source region stamps its temperature and humidity on the air.
normal.cn: 源地把温度与湿度印在空气上。

normal.en: The Bergen school linked air masses to fronts in the early twentieth century.
normal.cn: 卑尔根学派在 20 世纪初把气团与锋面联系起来。

normal.en: Modification explains why cold dry air can snow over a warm sea.
normal.cn: 气团变性解释了冷干空气为何能在暖海上致雪。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible blanket with a place-name printed on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看不见的毯子，上面印着一个地名。

abstract.en: Picture two crowds walking into each other and a line forming where they meet.
abstract.cn: 想象两群人迎面走来，在相接处形成一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a mood large enough to cover a whole electorate.
abstract.cn: 想象一种大到能盖住全体选民的情绪。

examples.en: The air mass was so uniform that radiosondes gave the same reading twice.
examples.cn: 该气团如此均匀，以致两次探空读数完全相同。

examples.en: Maritime air masses keep the coast mild in winter.
examples.cn: 海洋气团使海岸冬季温和。

examples.en: Two air masses met over the plain and produced a sharp line of showers.
examples.cn: 两个气团在平原上空相遇，形成一条清晰的阵雨带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「air（空气）+ mass（团块）」——一大团性质均匀的空气 → 气团

root: air 经拉丁 aer 出自希腊 aēr「低层空气」；mass 出自拉丁 massa「团块」，源出希腊 maza「面团」。复合词为 20 世纪初气象学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one body of air: the uniform volume, its source, its classification, its cold and warm types, its modification, the front it makes and finally any uniform bloc of people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一团空气：均匀的体积、源地、分类、冷与暖的类型、变性、与其他气团形成的锋，最后是任何同质的人群大块。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an invisible slab of air that carries the character of the ground it grew up on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块看不见的空气板，带着它生长之地的性格。

branches.en: BODY AND BIRTHPLACE: a uniform volume is defined by the region that made it uniform.
branches.cn: 体与出生地：均匀的体积由使它均匀的区域来定义。

branches.en: LABELS: latitude and surface classify it, and cold or warm is relative to the ground below.
branches.cn: 标签：纬度与下垫面给它分类，冷或暖相对于下方地面。

branches.en: CHANGE: nothing stays sealed; every surface exchanges heat and water with it.
branches.cn: 变化：没有东西是密封的；每个表面都与它交换热与水。

branches.en: CONTACT: a front is only the meeting place of two such bodies.
branches.cn: 接触：锋面只是两个这样气团的相遇处。

branches.en: METAPHOR: size and uniformity are lent to a crowd or a mood.
branches.cn: 比喻：体量与均匀性被借给人群或情绪。

intro.en: Air mass is a two-word technical compound, one Greek-derived word plus one Latin-derived word; its grammar is that of a noun phrase.
intro.cn: air mass 是双词技术复合语，由一个希腊来源词与一个拉丁来源词构成；其语法是名词短语。

latinIntro.en: Latin aer supplies air and Latin massa supplies mass; both are learned borrowings, not native roots.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aer 提供 air，拉丁 massa 提供 mass；两者都是学术借词，而非本族词根。

items.structure: air (noun from Latin aer, Greek aēr)
items.example: The air above the ice stayed dry.
items.exampleCN: 冰面上方的空气保持干燥。

items.structure: mass (noun from Latin massa, Greek maza)
items.example: A mass of cold air settled over the plain.
items.exampleCN: 一大团冷空气停在平原上空。

items.example: Air-mass boundaries show on the chart.
items.exampleCN: 气团边界显示在天气图上。

items.example: Polar air masses are cold and dry.
Tropical air masses carry much moisture.
items.exampleCN: 热带气团携带大量水汽。

items.example: The air-mass source lay over the steppe.
Air-mass modification warms the lower layer.

definition_zh: 生物量；生物质；生物质燃料
definition_en: the total mass of living matter in a given area, or living material used as fuel
core_image: 一整个生态系统被放上秤，读数就是活物的总重量
scene: 这里指「生物量」。 The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate the biomass of the meadow.
sceneCN: 这里 biomass 是「生物量」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的活物质总质量）；句意：研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物，以估算这片草甸的生物量。场景要点：样方框、电子秤、割下的草、记录板、烘干箱。

pos.zh: 生物量；（可作燃料的）生物质

senses.title: Total mass of living matter
senses.titleCN: 生物量：一个地区的活物质总量
senses.definition: the total mass of living organisms in a given area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 某一区域或体积内全部活物质的总质量
senses.example: The researchers weighed every plant in the plot to estimate biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员称量了样方里的每一株植物来估算生物量。
senses.why: bio- is 'life' and mass is 'a lump, a quantity of matter'. The compound simply asks how much living stuff there is, measured as mass rather than counted as individuals. The core image is a scale under an entire ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: bio- 是“生命”，mass 是“一团、一定量的物质”。这个复合词只问“活的东西有多少”，用质量来衡量，而不是数个体。核心意象是在整个生态系统下面放一台秤。

senses.title: Biomass of a species or population
senses.titleCN: 种群生物量：某一个物种的总重量
senses.definition: the total mass of one species or population in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种或种群在特定区域内的总质量
senses.example: The fish population's biomass fell by half in a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个鱼类种群的生物量十年间减少了一半。
senses.why: The total can be restricted to one group. The same measure is applied to a species, so biomass becomes a stock estimate rather than a whole-ecosystem figure, and fisheries use it to decide catch limits.
senses.whyCN: 总量可以被限定在一个群体上。同一把尺子用在一个物种上，biomass 就从“整个生态系统的数字”变成“资源存量估计”，渔业用它来定捕捞上限。

senses.title: Biomass at a trophic level
senses.titleCN: 营养级生物量：食物链每一层的重量
senses.definition: the mass of living matter grouped by trophic level in a food chain
senses.definitionCN: 按食物链营养级分组的活物质质量
senses.example: A pyramid of biomass shows less living matter at each higher level.
senses.exampleCN: 生物量金字塔显示，每高一层，活物质就越少。
senses.why: Ecologists arrange species by what they eat. Grouping biomass by trophic level turns a total into a structure, and the pyramid is the standard picture of that structure: producers below, predators above.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家按“吃什么”把物种排成层。把生物量按营养级分组，就把一个总数变成一种结构，而金字塔是这种结构的标准图像：生产者在下，捕食者在上。

senses.title: Plant or crop biomass
senses.titleCN: 植物与作物生物量：可收获的植物物质
senses.definition: the mass of plants or crops grown in a field, often measured to predict yield
senses.definitionCN: 田地里生长的植物或作物的质量，常用来预测产量
senses.example: Farmers measure above-ground biomass to predict the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 农民测量地上生物量来预测收成。
senses.why: Plants are the entry point of energy into an ecosystem, and their mass is what agriculture harvests. The compound therefore becomes a yield measure in agronomy, often qualified as above-ground or below-ground.
senses.whyCN: 植物是能量进入生态系统的入口，而农业收获的正是它们的质量。于是这个复合词在农学里成为产量指标，常以“地上／地下”来限定。

senses.title: Soil microbial biomass
senses.definition: the mass of microorganisms living in soil, used as an indicator of soil health
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中微生物的质量，用作土壤健康的指标
senses.example: Soil microbial biomass is a sensitive indicator of soil health.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤微生物生物量是土壤健康的一项敏感指标。
senses.why: Most living mass is invisible and below ground. Extending the word to microbes makes it a soil-health indicator, because microbes respond quickly to disturbance, fertilization and contamination.
senses.whyCN: 大部分活物质是看不见的，而且在地下。把词扩展到微生物，它就变成土壤健康指标，因为微生物对扰动、施肥和污染反应很快。

senses.title: Forest biomass and carbon stock
senses.definition: the mass of forest vegetation, especially as a measure of stored carbon
senses.definitionCN: 森林植被的质量，尤用作储存碳的度量
senses.example: The map estimates forest biomass to calculate stored carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图估算森林生物量，以计算储存的碳。
senses.why: About half of dry biomass is carbon, so weighing a forest also measures a carbon store. Climate policy made this technical equivalence central, and biomass became a number in carbon accounting.
senses.whyCN: 干生物量中约有一半是碳，所以给森林称重同时也在测量碳库。气候政策使这一技术等价关系变得关键，biomass 于是成为碳核算里的一个数字。

senses.title: Biomass as fuel feedstock
senses.titleCN: 生物质原料：可作燃料的生物材料
senses.definition: living or recently living material used as a source of fuel
senses.definitionCN: 用作燃料来源的活体或刚死去的生物材料
senses.example: The plant burns crop residues and wood chips as biomass.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把作物残余和木屑作为生物质燃烧。
senses.why: The word shifts from a measure to a material: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The physical substance, not the ecological total, is now the referent, and the word behaves like 'coal'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从“度量”转成“材料”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。此时指称的是实物，而不是生态总量，这个词在句中就像 coal 一样使用。

senses.title: Biomass power generation
senses.titleCN: 生物质发电：以生物质为燃料的技术
senses.definition: the use of biomass as fuel in boilers or power plants to produce heat and electricity
senses.definitionCN: 在锅炉或电厂中以生物质为燃料生产热与电
senses.example: A biomass plant supplies heat to the nearby town.
senses.exampleCN: 一座生物质电厂为附近的城镇供热。
senses.why: Once biomass is a fuel, it can be burned in a plant. The compound names the technology, and the word now belongs to engineering vocabulary as much as to ecology.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生物质成为燃料，就可以在电厂里燃烧。这个复合词命名的是一项技术，此时它既属于生态学词汇，也同样属于工程词汇。

senses.title: Biomass as a policy category
senses.titleCN: 政策口径中的生物质能
senses.definition: biomass counted as a renewable energy source in statistics and regulation
senses.definitionCN: 在统计与法规中被计为可再生能源的生物质
senses.example: Biomass counts as renewable in the national energy statistics.
senses.exampleCN: 在国家能源统计中，生物质被算作可再生能源。
senses.why: Policy needs categories. Biomass becomes an accounting box defined by origin rather than by ecology, and the word now answers a regulatory question: does this fuel count as renewable?
senses.whyCN: 政策需要分类。生物质于是变成一个按“来源”而非按“生态”定义的统计格子；这个词此时回答的是一个监管问题：这种燃料算不算可再生能源？

intro.en: Biomass is a 20th-century compound: Greek bio- 'life' joined to the Latin-derived English mass. It is not an inherited word, and the exact first coinage is uncertain; only the date by which it was in use is fairly well recorded.
intro.cn: biomass 是 20 世纪复合词：希腊语 bio-“生命”接上源自拉丁语的英语 mass。它不是承袭词，确切的首创情况存疑；只有“已在使用”的年代记录比较可靠。

items.en: bios means 'life, lifetime, way of life' (PIE *gwei- 'to live'). In scientific compounds bio- has meant 'organic life' since about 1800, and it is the first element of biomass.
items.cn: bios 意为“生命、寿命、生活方式”（原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”）。在科学复合词中，bio- 自约 1800 年起表示“有机生命”，是 biomass 的第一成分。

items.en: Latin massa means 'kneaded dough, lump, that which adheres together like dough', probably from Greek maza 'barley cake', related to massein 'to knead' (PIE *mag- 'to knead, fashion, fit').
items.cn: 拉丁 massa 意为“揉好的面团、团块、像面团那样黏在一起的东西”，可能来自希腊语 maza“大麦饼”，与 massein“揉”相关（原始印欧语 *mag-“揉、塑造、使合适”）。

items.en: English mass (late 14c) came from Old French masse and directly from Latin. It extended to 'a large quantity' in the 1580s, to 'bulk' about 1600, and to the physics sense 'quantity of matter' in 1704 — the sense biomass needs.
items.cn: 英语 mass（14 世纪晚期）来自古法语 masse，并直接借自拉丁语。16 世纪 80 年代扩展为“大量”，约 1600 年扩展为“体积、主体”，1704 年获得物理学义“物质的量”——正是 biomass 所需的那一层。

items.en: Etymonline records bio-mass 'by 1969' for 'the total weight of the organic substance or organisms in a given area'. Earlier uses may exist in mid-20th-century ecology and fisheries; the exact first coinage and first printed use are uncertain.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 bio-mass 记作“by 1969”，义为“某一区域内有机物质或生物的总重量”。20 世纪中期的生态学与渔业文献中可能有更早用法；确切首创与最早印刷记录存疑。

items.en: The modern energy sense moves from a measure to a commodity: what was counted as living mass becomes a stock of fuel. The link is practical — fuel is bought and sold by weight, so the measured mass turns into the traded substance.
items.cn: 现代能源义从“度量”转向“商品”：原本被计为活物质总量的东西，变成一堆燃料库存。联系是实用性的——燃料按重量买卖，于是被测量的质量变成了被交易的物质。

items.en: After the oil shocks of the 1970s, biomass entered energy policy as a renewable category alongside solar and wind. It is now standard in carbon accounting, bioenergy statistics and assessments of forest carbon stocks.
items.cn: 1970 年代石油危机之后，biomass 作为可再生能源类别与太阳能、风能并列进入能源政策。如今它已是碳核算、生物能源统计和森林碳储量评估中的标准词。

note.en: The first group contains bio- compounds and the base noun mass, which are easy to swap; the second contains ecological quantities that are often confused with biomass in measurement.
note.cn: 第一组是容易互换的 bio- 复合词与基础名词 mass；第二组是测量中常与 biomass 混淆的生态量。

entries.definition: A lump, a large quantity, or (in physics) the quantity of matter. Biomass adds bio- to restrict the mass to living material.
entries.definitionCN: 团块、大量，或物理学上的“物质的量”。biomass 加 bio- 把质量限定为活物质。

entries.definition: Gas produced by the breakdown of organic matter, mainly methane. It is a fuel made from biomass, not biomass itself.
entries.definitionCN: 有机物分解产生的气体，主要是甲烷。它是由生物质制成的燃料，而不是生物质本身。

entries.definition: Fuel made from living or recently living material. Biomass is the raw material; biofuel is the refined product.
entries.definitionCN: 由活体或刚死去的生物材料制成的燃料。biomass 是原料，biofuel 是加工后的产品。

entries.definition: The zone of life on Earth. It names a region, whereas biomass names a quantity within that region.
entries.definitionCN: 地球上的生命圈层。它命名一个区域，而 biomass 命名该区域内的一个量。

entries.definition: The amount of living matter present at a given moment. It is the actual measurement that a biomass estimate tries to represent.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻实际存在的活物量。它是 biomass 估计所试图表达的实际测量值。

entries.definition: The living organisms of a region as a group. It names the set of organisms, not their weight.
entries.definitionCN: 一个区域内作为整体的全部生物。它命名生物集合，而不是它们的重量。

entries.definition: Carbon-based material in soil or water, including dead and dissolved matter. Broader than biomass, which usually means living or recently living material.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或水中含碳的物质，包括死亡与溶解的部分。比 biomass 宽，后者通常指活的或刚死去的材料。

entries.definition: The amount harvested or produced, usually for human use. It measures what is taken, while biomass measures what is there.
entries.definitionCN: 收获或产出的量，通常供人使用。它衡量被取走的部分，而 biomass 衡量现存的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, the real mass family, and real measurement contrasts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的 mass 词族，以及真实的测量对比。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + mass 'lump of matter': life put on a scale and weighed.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ mass“一团物质”：把生命放上秤称重。

normal.en: mass has been in English since the late 14th century; the physics sense 'quantity of matter' dates from 1704 and is the one biomass uses.
normal.cn: mass 自 14 世纪晚期就在英语里；物理学义“物质的量”始于 1704 年，正是 biomass 所用的那一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. Same prefix, different question.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量数量，biodiversity 量多样。同一个前缀，不同的问题。

normal.en: Field convention: above-ground biomass and below-ground biomass are counted separately, so the word always needs a boundary.
normal.cn: 野外惯例：地上生物量与地下生物量分开计，所以这个词总需要一条边界。

normal.en: Energy chain: biomass (raw material) → biofuel or biogas (product) → bioenergy (the category).
normal.cn: 能源链：biomass（原料）→ biofuel 或 biogas（产品）→ bioenergy（类别）。

abstract.en: Picture an entire forest lifted onto an industrial scale; the number on the dial is biomass.
abstract.cn: 想象整片森林被抬上一台工业秤；表盘上的数字就是 biomass。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of trays, each holding less grain as you go up: that is the biomass pyramid.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞托盘堆成金字塔，越往上每一层的谷物越少：那就是生物量金字塔。

abstract.en: Picture a sack of wood chips beside a coal sack: both are fuel sold by weight, which is why 'mass' became 'biomass'.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋木屑放在一袋煤旁边：两者都是按重量卖的燃料，这正是“质量”变成“生物质”的原因。

examples.en: Tropical forests hold a large share of the world's living biomass.
examples.cn: 热带森林拥有全球活生物量的很大一部分。

examples.en: The village burns agricultural biomass instead of coal in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子冬天烧农业生物质而不是煤。

examples.en: Satellites can estimate forest biomass from the height and density of the canopy.
examples.cn: 卫星可以根据树冠的高度和密度估算森林生物量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命，欧（o）麦（m）斯（ss）——把生命放到秤上称重 → biomass 生物量、生物质

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 massa“面团、团块”演变来的 mass“质量”；20 世纪新造复合词，先指生态总量，后指可作燃料的生物质。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one measure: how much living matter there is. It is applied to a whole area, one species, one trophic level, one part of a plant, soil, or a forest; then the measured matter becomes a fuel, a technology, and a policy category.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一把尺子：活物质有多少。它被用于整片区域、一个物种、一个营养级、植物的一部分、土壤或森林；随后被测量之物又变成燃料、技术和政策类别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: living matter put on a scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：把活物质放上秤。

branches.en: WHAT IS WEIGHED: the whole community, or one species singled out as a stock.
branches.cn: 称的是什么：整个群落，或被单独拿出作为存量的一个物种。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: grouping by trophic level turns the total into a pyramid.
branches.cn: 结构：按营养级分组，把总量变成一个金字塔。

branches.en: POOLS: crops, soil microbes and forests are separate measured pools, and each has its own method.
branches.cn: 库：作物、土壤微生物与森林是各自独立的测量库，各有自己的方法。

branches.en: CONVERSION: measured matter becomes feedstock, then heat and electricity.
branches.cn: 转化：被测量的物质变成原料，再变成热与电。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: policy turns biomass into a renewable category with rules.
branches.cn: 核算：政策把生物质变成一个带规则的可再生类别。

intro.en: Biomass is a two-part modern compound: bio- + mass. Both halves are productive in English, so the word can be understood without knowing Latin or Greek; its compound status, not its age, is what makes it transparent.
intro.cn: biomass 是两段式现代复合词：bio- + mass。两半在英语里都能产，所以不懂拉丁语或希腊语也能理解；使它透明的，是复合词的身份，而不是年代。

latinIntro.en: Only the second element is Latin: massa 'kneaded dough, lump', probably from Greek maza. The first element is Greek bios. The compound was assembled in English, which is why no single Latin word corresponds to biomass.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第二成分是拉丁语：massa“面团、团块”，可能来自希腊语 maza。第一成分是希腊语 bios。这个复合词是在英语里拼合的，所以没有单个拉丁词与 biomass 对应。

definition_zh: 卑贱的；悲惨的；糟透的
definition_en: extremely low in condition, spirit, or quality; miserable
core_image: 被扔到门外的人，蜷在最低处的台阶上
scene: 失业又欠租，他站在粥棚队尾不敢抬头。 After losing everything, he lived in abject poverty for years.
sceneCN: 这里 abject 是「悲惨的、赤贫的」（第 2 个义项：处境极度低下）；句意为失去一切之后，他多年生活在赤贫之中。

pos.zh: 卑贱的；卑微的（形容处境）
悲惨的；糟透的（形容状态或品质）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「卑贱地；悲惨地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「卑贱；悲惨境况」

senses.title: Lacking self-respect
senses.definition: behaving in a way that shows no pride or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 表现出毫无骄傲或尊严的样子
senses.example: He made an abject apology for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他为延误低声下气地道歉。
senses.why: The Latin root jacere means to throw; a person thrown down and out lies at the lowest point, without standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 jacere 意为抛掷；被扔出去的人躺在最低处，站不起来。

senses.title: Extremely miserable in condition
senses.definition: in a state of extreme poverty, suffering, or misery
senses.definitionCN: 处于极度贫穷、痛苦或悲惨之中
senses.example: The refugees arrived in abject poverty and fear.
senses.exampleCN: 难民们带着赤贫与恐惧抵达。
senses.why: Being cast out strips everything; what is thrown away ends up in the worst condition.
senses.whyCN: 被抛出去意味着失去一切；被丢弃之物落得最坏的处境。

senses.title: Utterly bad in quality
senses.definition: of a quality or outcome, completely bad or without success
senses.definitionCN: 指品质或结果极差、毫无成功可言
senses.example: The campaign ended in abject failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动以彻底失败告终。
senses.why: The thrown-down image measures how low a result can sink; the worst outcome is the furthest down.
senses.whyCN: 「被抛落」的意象衡量结果能落到多低；最坏的结局就是坠得最深的那一个。

intro.en: Abject is Latin face to face: ab-, away, plus jacere, to throw; it describes what has been thrown out and down.
intro.cn: abject 是原样的拉丁语：ab-「离开」加 jacere「抛掷」；它描述被抛出去、摔到低处之物。

items.en: The root ye- meant to throw or hurl.
items.cn: 原始印欧词根 ye- 意为投掷。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw; abiectus was the participle, thrown away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 jacere 意为抛掷；abiectus 是其分词形式「被抛弃的」。

items.en: Abject passed through French as a learned adjective.
items.cn: abject 作为学术形容词经法语传递。

items.en: English adopted abject for the lowly and the miserable.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 abject，指卑下者与悲惨者。

items.en: It now intensifies nouns like poverty, fear, and failure.
items.cn: 如今它作强化语，修饰 poverty、fear、failure 等名词。

note.en: Abject belongs to the jac- throw family, which includes project and reject.
note.cn: abject 属于 jac-「抛掷」词族，project、reject 都在其中。

entries.definition: the noun meaning a miserable low state
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式，义为卑贱、悲惨境况

entries.definition: in a hopeless, servile way
to throw back or refuse
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝、退回；同根 jacere 但前缀不同

entries.definition: very unhappy or of very poor quality
behaving like a slave, overly eager to please
entries.definitionCN: 奴颜婢膝的；对应第 1 义项

entries.definition: without the basic means of life
entries.definitionCN: 一无所有的；对应赤贫义项

normalIntro.en: Five anchors tie abject to the thrown-down figure.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手把 abject 与被抛落的身影绑在一起。

normal.en: abject failure: as low as a result can go.

abstract.cn: 看见黑暗楼梯最低一级上的身影。

abstract.en: Feel mud at the bottom of a pit.
abstract.cn: 感到坑底烂泥的触感。

abstract.en: Hear the last coin drop from a torn pocket.
abstract.cn: 听见最后一枚硬币从破口袋坠落。

examples.en: They lived in abject poverty after the factory closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，他们生活在赤贫之中。

examples.en: His abject surrender shocked even his allies.
examples.cn: 他屈辱的投降连盟友都为之震惊。

examples.en: The team's abject performance cost the coach her job.
examples.cn: 球队糟透的表现让教练丢了工作。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses measure one fall: thrown-down pride, thrown-down fortune, thrown-down results.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项衡量同一次坠落：被抛下的尊严、被抛下的境遇、被抛下的结果。

branches.en: THE BENT BACK: dignity is the first thing thrown away.
branches.cn: 弯下的脊背：尊严是最先被抛弃的。

branches.en: THE EMPTY HANDS: fortune follows dignity to the bottom.

branches.en: ONE FALL: every sense is a depth below the ordinary line.

senses.why: A tall cabinet pouring its contents into a small box on a desk.
