abstract.cn: 一条进度条在旋转圆圈下一格一格填满。

examples.en: She waited for the file to download before leaving.
examples.cn: 她等文件下载完才离开。

examples.en: The download is saved in your music folder.
examples.cn: 下载的文件保存在你的音乐文件夹里。

examples.en: The download finished just as the train arrived.
examples.cn: 火车到站时下载刚好完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: download ＝ down（向下）＋ load（装载、负荷）＝「把一份负荷带下来」。早期计算机把数据从大型主机搬到本地小机器，就像从高处卸货，所以叫 download；今天它指把文件从网上复制到自己的设备。反方向是 upload（往上装）。名词也指下载到的文件和下载速度。

root: 古英语 dune（向下）＋ hladan（装载）→ load（负荷）→ 20 世纪计算机复合词 download（下载）

sensesIntro.en: A load brought down: an icon falling from a cloud, a finished file in a folder, a filling progress bar and a cabinet emptying into a small box.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份被带下来的负荷：从云端落下的图标、文件夹里完成的文件、填满的进度条与倒进小盒子的高柜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folder icon sliding down an arrow from a cloud onto a desktop while a progress bar fills block by block
core.cn: 核心意象：一个文件夹图标沿箭头从云端滑到桌面，同时进度条一格一格填满

branches.en: The act of bringing a file down.
branches.cn: 把文件带下来的动作。

branches.en: The file that has arrived.
branches.cn: 已经到达的文件。

branches.en: The process and how fast it runs.
branches.cn: 过程以及它跑得多快。

branches.en: An older move from host to local machine.
branches.cn: 从主机到本地机器的早期搬运。

branches.en: Both move data to a smaller system.
branches.cn: 两者都把数据移到较小的系统。

intro.en: Download is down plus load; up- reverses it into upload, and the Latin roots port- and fer- name carrying from another direction.
intro.cn: download 由 down 加 load 组成；up- 把它反转成 upload，而拉丁语词根 port- 与 fer- 从另一个方向指称搬运。

latinIntro.en: Latin portare means to carry, ferre to bear and onus a burden; ducere means to lead.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 portare 意为搬运，ferre 意为承担，onus 意为负担；ducere 意为引导。

definition_zh: adv. 一再地；持续不断地
definition_en: again and again, or without a pause
core_image: 表针一圈圈走着，看不出停下的时刻
scene: 他不停看表，一再问还要多久。 He continually checked his watch and asked how long it would take.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：continually 指一再地；句意是他反复看表追问时间。

senses.title: Again and again
senses.definition: happening over and over
senses.definitionCN: 一次又一次地发生
senses.example: He continually checks his phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他一遍遍看手机。
senses.why: A clock that keeps coming back to the same mark.
senses.whyCN: 表针一次次回到同一个刻度。

senses.title: Without a pause
senses.definition: going on without stopping
senses.definitionCN: 一直进行、不中断
senses.example: The river runs continually in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天河水不断地流。
senses.why: A tap that never fully closes.
senses.whyCN: 一直关不严的水龙头。

senses.title: As a nagging habit
senses.definition: so often that it annoys people
senses.definitionCN: 频繁到令人厌烦
senses.example: She is continually late.
senses.exampleCN: 她老是迟到。
senses.why: A dripping sound at night.
senses.whyCN: 夜里滴答不停的声响。

intro.en: Continually comes from Latin continuare, to join without a gap.
intro.cn: continually 来自拉丁语 continuare，意为无缝相接。

items.en: Continere means to hold together.
items.cn: continere 意为连在一起。

items.en: Continuus means unbroken, joined.
items.cn: continuus 意为未中断的、相连的。

items.en: Continuare means to make continuous.
items.cn: continuare 意为使连续。

items.en: Old French continuael carried the sense onward.
items.cn: 古法语 continuael 把这个意思传下来。

items.en: English split continual from continuous.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语把 continual 与 continuous 分开。

note.en: The look-alike group pairs the -al and -ous adverbs; the near-meaning group stresses repetition.
note.cn: 形近组对照 -al 与 -ous 两套副词；近义组强调反复。

entries.definition: Repeated over time.
Going on without a stop.
Without any break.
Very often or without stopping.
Over and over.
In a determined way.
Seemingly without stop.

normalIntro.en: Continually is the clock hand returning to the same mark.
normalIntro.cn: continually 就是表针一次次回到同一刻度。

normal.en: Continuare means to join without a gap.
normal.cn: continuare 意为无缝相接。

normal.en: Continual repeats, continuous does not stop.
normal.cn: continual 强调反复，continuous 强调不停。

normal.en: A continually ringing phone wears you down.
normal.cn: 响个不停的电话让人疲惫。

normal.en: Continually late is a bad habit.
normal.cn: 老是迟到是坏习惯。

normal.en: Spring rain falls continually.
normal.cn: 春雨绵绵不断。

abstract.en: A dripping tap at night.
abstract.cn: 夜里滴答的水龙头。

abstract.en: A clock hand circling again.
abstract.cn: 一圈又一圈的表针。

abstract.en: Footsteps pacing outside a door.
abstract.cn: 门外来回走的脚步。

examples.en: He continually interrupts the meeting.
examples.cn: 他不断打断会议。

examples.en: The team continually improves its design.
examples.cn: 团队不断改进设计。

examples.en: It rained continually for three days.
examples.cn: 雨一连下了三天。

dict_mnemonic.text: continue（继续）+ al（…的）+ ly（…地）→ 不断地、一再地。

root: 拉丁 continuus（不间断的）+ -al + -ly → 英语 continually

sensesIntro.en: A loop that comes around again, or a stream that does not stop.
sensesIntro.cn: 要么周而复始，要么源源不断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock hand circling back to the same mark
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈圈回到同一刻度的表针

branches.en: A phone that keeps ringing.
branches.cn: 响个不停的电话。

branches.en: A river that never pauses.
branches.cn: 从不停歇的河。

branches.en: A dripping tap at night.
branches.cn: 夜里滴答的水龙头。

branches.en: A habit repeated too often.
branches.cn: 重复过多的习惯。

branches.en: Rain falling for days.
branches.cn: 连下数日的雨。

intro.en: Continually stacks the adjective suffix -al and the adverb suffix -ly on the verb continue.
intro.cn: continually 在动词 continue 上依次加形容词后缀 -al 与副词后缀 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin continuus means unbroken.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 continuus 意为不间断的。

definition_zh: 恳求；郑重告诫；以誓言督促
definition_en: an urgent, solemn appeal made as if under oath
core_image: 长者在病榻前握着手恳切叮嘱
scene: 老人临别前握紧女儿的手，一字一句让她答应照顾弟弟。 His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
sceneCN: 这里 adjuration 是「恳求、郑重告诫」（第 1 个义项：仿佛发过誓般的恳切请求）；句意为他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「恳求；郑重命令」
同根近亲词，义为「发誓放弃」，方向相反

senses.title: A solemn urgent plea
senses.definition: an earnest appeal that presses the listener as if by oath
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛以誓言加身的恳切请求，逼着听者回应
senses.example: His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。
senses.why: Latin iurare means 'to swear'; to adjure is to swear at someone, wrapping the plea in oath-weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iurare 意为「发誓」；adjure 是把恳求裹上誓言的重量。

senses.title: A command backed by oath
senses.definition: a solemn command made under or with appeal to an oath
senses.definitionCN: 借助或伴随誓言发出的郑重命令
senses.example: The witness acted under adjuration to tell the whole truth.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在责令之下说出全部真相。
senses.why: When the plea hardens into duty, the appeal becomes a command the oath enforces.
senses.whyCN: 当恳求硬化为义务，请求就变成誓言所强制的命令。

intro.en: Adjuration comes from Latin adjurare, 'to swear to', from ad- 'to' plus iurare 'to swear'.
intro.cn: adjuration 来自拉丁语 adjurare（对……起誓），由 ad-（向）加 iurare（发誓）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *yewes- is thought to relate to sacred speech; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *yewes- 与神圣言辞相关；此说尚存疑。

items.en: ius meant 'law, oath'; iurare meant 'to swear'.
items.cn: ius 意为「法、誓」；iurare 意为「发誓」。

items.en: adjurare meant 'to swear to, to charge under oath'.
items.cn: adjurare 意为「对……起誓、以誓责令」。

items.en: English adjuration entered through religious and legal texts.
items.cn: 英语 adjuration 经宗教与法律文本进入。

items.en: Now rare and literary; everyday speech prefers earnest plea.
items.cn: 如今罕见而书面化；日常用语多用 earnest plea。

note.en: The first group gathers the iurare family; the second gathers words for solemn appeal.
note.cn: 第一组收 iurare 词族；第二组收表示郑重恳求的词。

entries.definition: The parent verb, to charge solemnly as if under oath.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「郑重恳求、誓令」，本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: To swear away, to renounce under oath; one letter apart, opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「誓绝、放弃」；一字母之差，方向相反。

entries.definition: False swearing; same root with a hostile prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伪证」；同根，前缀带敌意。

entries.definition: An earnest plea without the oath element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恳求」，不含誓言成分。

entries.definition: Strong urging toward action.
A spoken curse; oath-word turned hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咒骂」，誓言词的敌意面。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the swear root iurare and the deathbed scene; the abstract hooks picture hands pressed to close a promise.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「发誓」词根 iurare 与病榻场景；抽象记忆点想象握紧的手封存承诺。

normal.en: Adjuration is ad- plus iurare: an oath pressed upon you.
normal.cn: adjuration 是 ad- 加 iurare：压到你身上的誓言。

normal.en: The verb is adjure.
normal.cn: 动词是 adjure。

normal.en: Abjure turns the oath around: to swear away.
normal.cn: abjure 把誓言反过来：发誓放弃。

normal.en: Perjury is the criminal cousin: false oath.
normal.cn: perjury 是犯罪的亲戚：假誓。

normal.en: The word is literary; use plea in speech.
normal.cn: 这个词很书面；口语用 plea。

abstract.en: Picture hands clasped tight around a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象双手紧握封存一个承诺。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand as the plea is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象恳求说出时举起的手。

abstract.en: Picture a will signed with a final whispered charge.
abstract.cn: 想象遗嘱签定时最后一声耳语叮嘱。

examples.en: His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
examples.cn: 他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。

examples.en: The priest's adjuration moved the crowd to silence.
examples.cn: 神父的郑重告诫让人群安静下来。

examples.en: The witness acted under adjuration to tell the whole truth.
examples.cn: 证人在责令之下说出全部真相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额决瑞申」——额头上顶着决绝的誓言申请，就是誓令般的恳求。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ iurare（发誓）→ adjurare（以誓责令）；核心义是「把誓言的重量压在恳求上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the oath-weighted plea, to the command that the oath enforces.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从裹着誓言的恳求，走到誓言所强制的命令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oath wrapped around a plea
core.cn: 核心意象：裹着誓言的恳求

branches.en: The urgent plea that weighs like an oath.
branches.cn: 重如誓言的急切恳求。

branches.en: The command the oath turns the plea into.
branches.cn: 恳求经誓言硬化成的命令。

branches.en: Both senses carry the same oath-weight.
branches.cn: 两个义项带着同一份誓言之重。

branches.en: Religious and legal texts are its native ground.
branches.cn: 宗教与法律文本是它的原生土壤。

branches.en: Both rest on iurare, the Latin verb of swearing.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「发誓」动词 iurare。

intro.en: The noun joins ad- with the swear-root jur- through the -ation ending, and the family spreads into jury, justice, and abjure.
intro.cn: 这个名词经词尾 -ation 把 ad- 与「发誓」词根 jur- 结合，词族延伸到 jury、justice 与 abjure。

latinIntro.en: Latin iurare and adjurare are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 iurare 与 adjurare。

items.meaning: that which the law and oath serve

latinEntries.meaning: to swear to, to charge under oath

definition_zh: 美容师；护肤专家；美学家（亦作 esthetician）
definition_en: a person trained in skin care and beauty treatment; also a specialist in the philosophy of beauty, more often spelled esthetician in American use
core_image: 专门打理「看起来如何」的那个人
scene: 护理室的灯调得很柔，她先看了看客人的皮肤再开口。 The aesthetician recommended a gentler routine.
sceneCN: 这里 aesthetician 是「美容师」（第 1 个义项：受过皮肤护理与美容训练的专业人员）；句意为美容师建议了一套更温和的护理流程。核心画面是专门打理「看起来如何」的那个人。

pos.zh: 美容师；护肤专家；美学家

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ian 的形容词，义为「审美的；美学的」
加 -s 构成，义为「美学；审美观」
加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美上」

senses.title: A specialist in skin care and beauty treatment
senses.definition: a person professionally trained to treat and care for the skin, especially the face
senses.definitionCN: 受过专业训练、从事皮肤（尤指面部）护理与治疗的人
senses.example: The aesthetician explained which acids suited sensitive skin.
senses.exampleCN: 美容师解释了哪些酸类适合敏感肌。
senses.why: Aisthetikos means able to perceive, so an aesthetician is literally a person who works on what is perceived, which in a salon means the surface others see.
senses.whyCN: aisthetikos 意为「能感知的」，所以 aesthetician 字面上是「打理被感知之物的人」，在美容院里就是别人看得见的那层表面。

senses.title: A specialist in the philosophy of beauty
senses.definition: a scholar who studies beauty and taste, a sense closer to the original philosophical use of aesthetic
senses.definitionCN: 研究美与趣味的学者，此义更接近 aesthetic 最初的哲学用法
senses.example: The aesthetician argued that ugliness has its own grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 那位美学家主张丑也有自己的语法。
senses.why: This sense keeps the word on its older path: the same perceiving root applied to judging art rather than to treating skin.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项让词留在更古老的路上：同一个「感知」词根用于评判艺术，而非护理皮肤。

intro.en: Aesthetician grew out of a Greek word for perceiving, and it split into two careers: one in a salon, one in a study.
intro.cn: aesthetician 源自一个表示「感知」的希腊语词，后来分成两种职业：一种在美容院，一种在书房。

items.en: Greek aisthanesthai meant to perceive or to feel, the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: 希腊语 aisthanesthai 意为「感知、感觉」，是整个词族背后的动词。

items.en: Greek aisthetikos meant perceptive or sensitive, built on the verb of perceiving.
items.cn: 希腊语 aisthetikos 意为「有感知力的、敏感的」，建立在感知动词上。

items.en: Aesthetic entered English in the eighteenth century through German discussions of beauty and taste.
items.cn: aesthetic 于十八世纪经德语关于美与趣味的讨论进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ian names a person practising or expert in something, as in musician and physician.
items.cn: 后缀 -ian 表示从事或精通某事的人，如 musician、physician。

items.en: Aesthetician is recorded from the nineteenth century; in twentieth century American use it narrowed mainly to skin care, often spelled esthetician.
items.cn: aesthetician 见于十九世纪；在二十世纪美式用法中主要收窄为皮肤护理，常拼作 esthetician。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the perceiving family, including the spelling without the a; the near-meaning group lists other skin and beauty professionals.
note.cn: 形近组留在「感知」词族内，包括省去 a 的拼写；近义组列出其他皮肤与美容专业人员。

entries.definition: Concerned with beauty and the appreciation of it.
The usual American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的美式常用拼写。

entries.definition: A drug that removes sensation, with an- meaning without.
entries.definitionCN: 消除感觉的药物，an- 表示「无」。

entries.definition: A person whose job is beauty treatment, a broader term.
entries.definitionCN: 以美容为业的人，含义更宽。

entries.definition: A professional trained in cosmetic treatment of skin, hair and nails.
entries.definitionCN: 受过皮肤、毛发与指甲美容训练的专业人员。

entries.definition: A doctor specializing in skin disease rather than beauty care.
entries.definitionCN: 专治皮肤疾病而非美容护理的医生。

normalIntro.en: Aesthetician is aesthetic plus -ian: the person who does aesthetics, whether on a face or in a book.
normalIntro.cn: aesthetician 就是 aesthetic 加 -ian：做美学这件事的人，无论在脸上还是在书里。

normal.en: Music plus -ian gives musician; aesthetic plus -ian gives aesthetician.
normal.cn: music 加 -ian 得 musician；aesthetic 加 -ian 得 aesthetician。

normal.en: The aes- at the front is the same as in anaesthetic, only without the negation.
normal.cn: 词首的 aes- 与 anaesthetic 中相同，只是没有否定前缀。

normal.en: In American salons you will usually see esthetician without the a.
normal.cn: 在美式美容院里你通常会看到省去 a 的 esthetician。

normal.en: An aesthetician treats skin; a dermatologist treats disease.
normal.cn: aesthetician 护理皮肤；dermatologist 治疗疾病。

normal.en: The older sense is a thinker about beauty, not a treater of faces.
normal.cn: 更古老的义项是思考美的人，而不是护理脸的人。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose whole job is the surface that others perceive.
abstract.cn: 想象一个全部工作就是别人所感知的那层表面的人。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp turned low so that every texture can be judged fairly.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏调暗的灯，让每种质地都能被公平评判。

abstract.en: Think of the same word walking from a philosophy lecture into a treatment room.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词从哲学讲堂走进护理室。

examples.en: The aesthetician kept a record of every product she used.
examples.cn: 美容师记录了她使用的每一种产品。

examples.en: An aesthetician must understand both chemistry and skin.
examples.cn: 美容师必须同时懂化学与皮肤。

examples.en: The eighteenth century aesthetician wrote only about taste.
examples.cn: 十八世纪的美学家只写趣味问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱斯塞提申」——爱（aes）斯（the）塞（ti）提申（cian），专门打理「看起来怎样」的那个人，就是美容师、美学家。

root: 希腊语 aisthanesthai「感知」派生 aisthetikos「有感知力的」，经德语美学讨论进入英语 aesthetic，再加表示人的后缀 -ian 构成 aesthetician，字面即「从事感知与美的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses share one root idea of perceiving: one works on the surface that is perceived, the other on the judgement of what is perceived.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共享「感知」这一词根想法：一个打理被感知的表面，另一个研究对被感知之物的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who works on what is perceived
core.cn: 核心意象：打理被感知之物的人

branches.en: Perceiving applied to skin as a surface.
branches.cn: 把感知用于作为表面的皮肤。

branches.en: Perceiving applied to judging art.
branches.cn: 把感知用于评判艺术。

branches.en: Both keep the Greek root of sensation.
branches.cn: 两者都保留希腊语「感觉」词根。

branches.en: The narrower modern American career.
branches.cn: 更窄的现代美式职业。

branches.en: The older philosophical career.
branches.cn: 更古老的哲学职业。

intro.en: Aesthetician is a Greek root of sensation plus a person suffix, and negating the same root produces the word for losing feeling.
intro.cn: aesthetician 是希腊语「感觉」词根加表人后缀，而否定同一词根就得到表示失去感觉的词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek aisthesis, sensation; Latin borrowed it as aesthesis, which is why the spelling keeps the aes- cluster.

definition_zh: n. 轻视，蔑视；藐视（法庭）
definition_en: a feeling that someone or something is worthless

definition_zh: v. 阐明；解释；使清楚；阐释
definition_en: to make something clear by explaining it
core_image: 一束手电光扫过写满术语的黑板，每照到一行，旁边就浮出一句白话解释
scene: 研讨室里投影上是一页密密麻麻的公式，主讲人拿起激光笔逐行点过去，把每个符号换成一句白话。 The diagram helped to elucidate the mechanism of the reaction.
sceneCN: 这里 elucidate 指「阐明」（第 1 个义项：把难懂的内容讲清楚）；句意是那张示意图帮助阐明了反应机理。

senses.title: To make clear
senses.definition: to explain something so that it becomes clear

senses.exampleCN: 老师用一张图就把这条规则阐明了。
senses.why: A torch beam crossing a blackboard until every symbol has a plain sentence beside it

senses.title: To shed light on a text

senses.exampleCN: 一条脚注阐释了诗中那个古词。

senses.title: To clarify by detail

senses.why: A sketch map with three numbered stops added one at a time

intro.en: Elucidate comes from Latin e- meaning out and lucidus meaning bright, from lux meaning light; to elucidate is to bring a thing out into the light.
intro.cn: elucidate 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 lucidus（明亮的），后者源自 lux（光）；elucidate 就是把事物带到光下。

items.en: Lux means light, the source of lucidus and of many English words about brightness.
items.cn: lux 意为光，是 lucidus 的来源，也是英语中许多与光亮有关词语的源头。

items.en: Lucidus means bright or clear, and gives English lucid.
items.cn: lucidus 意为明亮或清楚，给出英语 lucid。

items.en: Late Latin elucidare means to make clear, built from e- plus lucidus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 elucidare 意为使清楚，由 e- 加 lucidus 构成。

items.en: English takes elucidate in the 1560s for explaining a difficult text.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 60 年代吸收 elucidate，用于解释难懂的文本。

items.en: The noun elucidation becomes common in scholarly commentary.
items.cn: 名词 elucidation 在学术注释中变得常见。

items.en: Researchers elucidate mechanisms and structures, extending the word to science.
items.cn: 研究者阐明机理与结构，把这个词扩展到科学领域。

note.en: Elucidate, illuminate and lucid all share the Latin root for light; clarify and explain are the everyday equivalents.
note.cn: elucidate、illuminate 与 lucid 共享拉丁语「光」的词根；clarify 与 explain 是日常对应词。

examples.en: He elucidated the proposal with three case studies from the pilot year.

dict_mnemonic.text: elucidate ＝ e-（向外）＋ lucid（清楚的，拉丁 lucidus「明亮」，源自 lux「光」）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝「把东西搬到光下」。名词 elucidation，同根形容词 lucid 清楚的、名词 lucidity 清晰、translucent 半透明的、illuminate 照亮。及物动词，宾语是难懂的内容：elucidate a point 阐明论点、elucidate the mechanism 阐明机理、elucidate a text 阐释文本。常用于学术与科技写作，语气比 explain 正式。近义 clarify 侧重消除混乱，explicate 侧重逐层展开文本，interpret 侧重给出意义；elucidate 强调用光照亮式的讲明白。

root: 拉丁语 e-（向外）＋ lucidus（明亮的，源自 lux「光」）→ elucidare（使清楚）→ elucidate（阐明）

definition_zh: 祸根；毒物；克星；造成痛苦之源
definition_en: a cause of harm, death, or misery; a poison
core_image: 毒草挂在名字后面：谁碰谁遭殃
scene: 园丁指着一丛白色毒芹摇头叹息。 Wolfsbane is the bane of grazing cattle.
sceneCN: 这里 bane 指「毒物、克星」（第 2 个义项：致害之物）；句意：狼毒乌头是吃草牛的克星。

collocations.zh: 令我深恶痛绝之物；克星

senses.title: A cause of ruin or misery
senses.definition: something that constantly causes trouble or suffering
senses.definitionCN: 不断带来麻烦或痛苦的东西
senses.example: Noise became the bane of her life.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音成了她一生的祸根。
senses.why: Old English bana meant a slayer; the slayer softens into the tormentor.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bana 意为「杀戮者」；杀戮者渐弱化为折磨者。

senses.title: A poison
senses.definition: a poison that kills, especially of plants
senses.definitionCN: 致死之毒，多指毒草
senses.example: Hemlock was the bane of Socrates.
senses.exampleCN: 毒芹是苏格拉底的死亡之毒。
senses.why: The literal slayer is the poison itself.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的「杀戮者」即毒物本身。

senses.title: In plant names
senses.definition: a second element in names of poisonous plants, as wolfsbane and henbane
senses.definitionCN: 毒草名称的后缀成分，如 wolfsbane、henbane
senses.example: Henbane grows along the hedge.
senses.exampleCN: 天仙子沿篱笆生长。
senses.why: Old herbals labeled each poison by its victim: wolf's bane kills wolves.
senses.whyCN: 古老草药书按受害者命名毒草：狼之毒、母鸡之毒。

senses.title: A natural enemy
senses.definition: the thing or person that reliably defeats another
senses.definitionCN: 总能克制对手的事物或人
senses.example: Quick wits are the bane of a bully.
senses.exampleCN: 急智是恶霸的克星。
senses.why: What kills the wolf becomes what defeats the type.
senses.whyCN: 能杀狼之物引申为能克制其类者。

senses.title: The adjective baneful
senses.definition: harmful or destructive in effect
senses.definitionCN: 效果上有害的、毁灭性的
senses.example: Baneful habits crept into his routine.
senses.exampleCN: 有害的习惯悄悄潜入他的日常。
senses.why: The suffix -ful turns the poison into a quality.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 把毒物化为性质。

senses.title: Literary ruin
senses.definition: destruction or death in elevated or old-fashioned style
senses.definitionCN: 书面或古雅语体中的毁灭、死亡
senses.example: The poet sang of the hero's bane.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人咏唱英雄的殒灭。
senses.why: Epic verse kept the old slaying word alive.
senses.whyCN: 史诗韵文让古老的杀戮词存活下来。

senses.title: Compound with things and vermin
senses.definition: compounds naming pest killers, as ratsbane and bugbane
senses.definitionCN: 指杀灭害虫之物的复合词，如 ratsbane、bugbane
senses.example: Ratsbane was scattered in the granary.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓里撒了灭鼠药。
senses.why: The naming pattern of plant names spread to pest poisons.
senses.whyCN: 毒草命名模式扩展到灭害之毒。

senses.title: Ironical everyday use
senses.definition: a jocular way to blame a minor annoyance
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑地归咎于小烦恼的说法
senses.example: Monday mornings are the bane of my existence.
senses.exampleCN: 周一早晨是我命中克星。
senses.why: Grand ruin shrunk to comic complaint.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的毁灭缩成喜剧式的抱怨。

intro.en: Bane goes back to Old English bana, a slayer, from a Germanic root meaning to kill; the poison sense and the tormentor sense both grow from the killer.
intro.cn: bane 源自古英语 bana「杀戮者」，出日耳曼语「杀」之词根；「毒物」与「折磨者」二义皆由「杀者」生出。

items.en: A Germanic verb *banon meant to kill, to slay.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼动词 *banon 意为杀、戮。

items.en: bana named a slayer, murderer, or the devil as the murderer of souls.
items.cn: 古英语 bana 指杀人者，亦指谋害灵魂的魔鬼。

items.en: The word came to mean poison, as in ratsbane and henbane.
items.cn: 中古英语转指毒物，如 ratsbane、henbane。

items.en: Poetry kept the ruin sense; herbals kept the plant compounds.
items.cn: 诗歌保留毁灭义；草药书保留植物复合词。

items.en: Today the word lives chiefly in the phrase the bane of, a fixed complaint.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词主要存活于 the bane of 的固定抱怨句式。

note.en: Group one holds the slayer family and look-alikes; group two holds the harm field.
note.cn: 第一组收「杀戮」词族与形近词；第二组收「为害」义场。

core_image: 中间人一手牵买家一手牵卖家，从成交里抽一小截
scene: 交易大厅里电话声此起彼伏，报价屏不停闪烁。 Her brokerage handled trades for two hundred clients.
sceneCN: 这里 brokerage 是「经纪公司」（第 2 个义项：经营代理买卖业务的公司）；句意是她所在的经纪公司为两百名客户打理交易。

pos.zh: 经纪业务；经纪公司；经纪人佣金

derivatives.zh: brokerage 的基础词，义为「经纪人；掮客」
由 broker 加 -ship 构成，义为「经纪身份；经纪行当（罕用）」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「居间撮合的行为」

senses.title: The broker's business
senses.definition: the trade of acting as an agent between buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 在买卖双方之间居间代理的业务
senses.example: The firm moved from banking into brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从银行业转入了经纪业务。
senses.why: The agent suffix -age turns the broker into his line of work.
senses.whyCN: 集体或行为后缀 -age 把经纪人转成他的业务行当。

senses.title: A firm of brokers
senses.definition: a company whose business is brokerage
senses.definitionCN: 经营经纪业务的公司机构
senses.example: She opened an account at a discount brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家折扣券商开了账户。
senses.why: A business name easily becomes the name of the business place.
senses.whyCN: 业务的名称顺势转指经营这项业务的机构。

senses.title: The broker's fee
senses.definition: the fee or commission charged for arranging a deal
senses.definitionCN: 为撮合交易而收取的酬金
senses.example: The deal cost them a hefty brokerage.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易让他们付了一笔可观的佣金。
senses.why: -age also names payment for a service, like postage orstorage.
senses.whyCN: -age 也可表服务酬金，如 postage、storage 之类。

intro.en: Brokerage is broker plus -age, and broker itself comes from an Old French word for small trader.
intro.cn: brokerage 由 broker 加 -age 构成，broker 则源自古法语指小贩的词。

items.en: broceour meant a small trader, wine seller or retailer.
items.cn: 古法语 broceour 指小贩、酒贩或零售商。

items.en: brocour crossed into England with the wine trade.
items.cn: 随酒业传入英格兰，词形作 brocour。

items.en: broker meant a middleman in trade, at first with a hint of trickery.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 broker 指居间商人，起初略带贬义。

items.en: brokerage formed on broker with the -age suffix for business and fees.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪以 broker 加 -age 构成 brokerage，兼指业务与佣金。

items.en: brokerage now names firms, accounts and fees in finance and property.
items.cn: 如今 brokerage 用于金融与地产，指券商、账户与佣金。

note.en: Brokerage belongs to the world of agents and middlemen.
note.cn: brokerage 属于代理与居间业务的世界。

entries.definition: an agent who buys and sells for others
the act of arranging deals as a broker
the fee or act of storing
entries.definitionCN: 仓储（费）——同为 -age 表费用，词根不同

entries.definition: the business of acting for others; an agent's firm
a fee paid as a percentage of a sale
a trader who buys and sells on his own account
a person who acts between two parties
a business company

normalIntro.en: Stack the word: broker plus age equals the broker's business, firm and fee.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆开记：broker 加 age，即经纪人的业务、公司与佣金。

normal.en: Broker + age: like postage, a fee word.
normal.cn: broker 加 -age，如 postage 一样可表费用。

normal.en: A brokerage account is where the broker works for you.
normal.cn: brokerage account 就是券商替你操作交易的账户。

normal.en: Real estate brokerage sells houses for a cut.
normal.cn: 地产中介抽成卖房。

normal.en: Dealer trades his own goods; broker trades yours.
normal.cn: dealer 卖自己的货，broker 卖你的货。

normal.en: Age here means business, not years.
normal.cn: 这里的 -age 表业务，与年龄无关。

abstract.en: See a middleman shaking two hands at once.
abstract.cn: 想象中间人同时握住两只手。

abstract.en: Watch a thin slice peel off every big deal.
abstract.cn: 看着每笔大交易上削下薄薄一片。

abstract.en: Hear ringing phones in a room full of screens.
abstract.cn: 听满屋屏幕间电话铃声大作。

examples.en: The brokerage earned a fee on every share traded.
examples.cn: 券商从每笔股票交易中抽取佣金。

examples.en: He left banking to open a small brokerage downtown.
examples.cn: 他离开银行业，在市中心开了家小经纪行。

examples.en: They cut brokerage costs by trading online.
examples.cn: 他们改做线上交易以省下经纪费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不若亏之」——中间人劝你：「不若亏之」，亏他一点佣金，买卖才成。

root: brokerage 由 broker（经纪人）加 -age（业务、费用）构成；broker 源自古法语 broceour／brocour（小贩、酒商），更早词源不确定，或与灌木丛（broce）中摆摊的零售者有关，属存疑假说。

sensesIntro.en: The -age suffix spreads one root across the business, the firm and the fee.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个 -age 后缀，让同一个词根覆盖了业务、公司和佣金三义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a middleman taking a thin slice of the deal.
core.cn: 核心意象：中间人从成交中抽走薄薄一片。

branches.en: go into brokerage
branches.cn: 进入经纪行业

branches.en: an insurance brokerage
branches.cn: 保险经纪行

branches.en: a brokerage account
branches.cn: 券商账户

branches.cn: 收取高额佣金

branches.cn: 该笔交易的佣金

intro.cn: 词族不大：经纪人、其行为、其身份、其业务。

latinIntro.en: The trail is French and possibly older still, ending in uncertainty.
latinIntro.cn: 词源经法语上溯，更早来源不确定。

definition_zh: n. 垮台；衰败；祸根；堕落；（旧）暴雨，大雪
definition_en: a sudden loss of power or position, the thing that causes ruin, or a heavy fall of rain
core_image: 王座上的雕像从基座翻落摔碎；一根被抽掉的支柱让整排架子塌下；一片乌云把整桶雨水倒在山谷上
scene: 王座上的雕像从基座翻落，在台阶上摔成几块。 The statue toppled from its pedestal, a fitting image of the downfall of the regime.
sceneCN: 这里 downfall 是「垮台」（第 1 个义项：统治者或政权突然失去权力与地位）；句意是雕像从基座翻落，正好是这个政权垮台的写照。图中可辨识物件：王座基座、翻落的雕像、碎裂的石块、台阶。

pos.zh: 垮台；衰败；祸根；堕落；（旧）暴雨，大雪

senses.title: Loss of power
senses.definition: the sudden loss of power or position by a ruler or government
senses.definitionCN: （名词）统治者或政府突然失去权力或地位
senses.example: The scandal led to the downfall of the minister.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻导致这位部长垮台。
senses.why: A statue toppling from its pedestal and breaking on the steps.
senses.whyCN: 一座雕像从基座翻落，在台阶上摔碎。

senses.title: The cause of ruin
senses.definition: the thing that causes someone to fail or be ruined
senses.definitionCN: （名词）导致某人失败或毁灭的事物
senses.example: Greed proved to be his downfall.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪成了他的祸根。
senses.why: One support knocked out from under a loaded shelf.
senses.whyCN: 满载架子下被抽掉的一根支柱。

senses.title: A moral fall
senses.definition: a fall from a high moral state into wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: （名词）从高尚的道德状态跌入恶行
senses.example: The novel traces the downfall of an honest man.
senses.exampleCN: 小说追溯了一个诚实人的堕落。
senses.why: A white robe dragged through mud until it is grey.
senses.whyCN: 一件白袍被拖过泥地，直到变成灰色。

senses.title: A heavy fall of rain
senses.definition: a heavy fall of rain or snow, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: （名词）旧时或文学用法中指雨或雪的大量降落
senses.example: A sudden downfall of rain flooded the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一场骤降的大雨淹了院子。
senses.why: A cloud tipping a whole bucket of water over a valley.
senses.whyCN: 一片乌云把整桶水倒在山谷上。

intro.en: Downfall is down plus fall, a falling down; it first named a literal drop, then the drop of a ruler from power, and in older writing a heavy fall of rain.
intro.cn: downfall 由 down 加 fall 组成，就是「往下落」；它先指实际的坠落，再指统治者从权位上跌落，旧时文字里也指雨的大量降落。

items.en: Old English dune means down or downward.
items.cn: 古英语 dune 意为向下。

items.en: Old English feallan means to fall.
items.cn: 古英语 feallan 意为落下。

items.en: Middle English downfall names a literal falling down.
items.cn: 中古英语 downfall 指实际的坠落。

items.en: The word is used for a ruler losing position.
items.cn: 这个词被用于统治者失去权位。

items.en: Writers use downfall for a heavy fall of rain or snow.
items.cn: 作者用 downfall 指雨或雪的大量降落。

items.en: Downfall now most often names ruin or the cause of ruin.
items.cn: downfall 现在最常指垮台或导致垮台的原因。

note.en: Downfall is a falling down; its look-alikes share down or fall, and its neighbours name other ways a high position ends.
note.cn: downfall 是往下落；形近词共用 down 或 fall，近义词则是高位终结的其他方式。

to reduce the size of a workforce
looking down, or feeling low

entries.definition: to fall down or fail suddenly
the state of being destroyed or bankrupt

dict_mnemonic.text: downfall ＝ down（向下）＋ fall（落下）＝「往下落」。先是实际的坠落，再是统治者从权位上跌落，即垮台；也指把人拖垮的那件事，即祸根。旧时文字里还指雨的大量降落，今天这个意思多用 downpour。

root: 古英语 dune（向下）＋ feallan（落下）→ 中古英语 downfall（坠落）→ 现代 downfall（垮台；祸根；旧指暴雨）

sensesIntro.en: One thing high coming down: a statue off its pedestal, a support knocked out, a robe in mud and a cloud emptying over a valley.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个高处之物落下来：离开基座的雕像、被抽掉的支柱、泥里的白袍与倒空在山谷上的乌云。

branches.en: A fall in conduct rather than rank.

branches.en: Rain falling in one heavy drop.

branches.en: The fall itself and the cause of it.
branches.cn: 跌落本身与跌落的原因。

intro.en: Downfall is down plus fall; -en builds fallen, and the Latin roots ru- and cad- name falling from another direction.
intro.cn: downfall 由 down 加 fall 组成；-en 造出 fallen，而拉丁语词根 ru- 与 cad- 从另一个方向指称落下。

latinIntro.en: Latin ruere means to rush down, cadere to fall and casus a fall; imber means a rain storm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ruere 意为冲落，cadere 意为落下，casus 意为一次坠落；imber 意为暴雨。

definition_zh: v. 使集中；把…集中到中央；实行集中管理
definition_en: to bring power, control or activity together under one centre
core_image: 四个仓库的钥匙交到同一张桌上
scene: 公司决定把四个仓库的库存集中到一个系统里。 The company decided to centralize stock from four warehouses.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：centralize 指使集中；句意是公司把四个仓库的库存集中到一个系统。

senses.title: To bring under one control
senses.definition: to move decision-making or control into a single authority
senses.definitionCN: 把决策或控制权移入单一机构
senses.example: The ministry centralized all approvals.
senses.exampleCN: 该部把所有审批权集中起来。
senses.why: The verb is centre plus the suffix meaning to make.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 centre 加上表示「使…」的词缀。

senses.title: To gather in one place
senses.definition: to move records, stock or equipment into one place
senses.definitionCN: 把档案、库存或设备移到一处
senses.example: They centralized the archive in the basement.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把档案集中到地下室。
senses.why: The physical sense follows from the same inward movement.
senses.whyCN: 实物含义同样源于向内收拢的动作。

intro.en: Centralize is centre plus a verb suffix, built on Latin centrum.
intro.cn: centralize 是 centre 加动词词缀，建于拉丁语 centrum 之上。

items.en: Centrum names the middle point.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centrum 指中心点。

items.en: Central enters English meaning of the middle.
items.cn: 十七世纪 central 进入英语，意为居中的。

items.en: The verb means to place in the middle.
items.cn: 十八世纪动词意为置于中央。

items.en: Centralize names the gathering of office power.
items.cn: 十九世纪指把机关权力收归一处。

items.en: Firms centralize buying and records.
items.cn: 二十世纪企业集中采购与档案。

items.en: Centralize covers any inward gathering.
items.cn: 现代泛指任何向内集中。

note.en: The look-alike group varies the ending; the near-meaning group names gathering and its reverse.
note.cn: 形近组变化词尾；近义组列出聚集及其反面。

normal.en: Power and records move inward.

normal.en: Its reverse adds de- in front.

examples.en: They centralized the files in one office.
examples.cn: 他们把档案集中到一间办公室。

examples.en: Centralizing decisions slowed the local branches.
examples.cn: 把决策集中拖慢了地方分部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森戳来子」——森林里把东西戳到中央，摞成一叠子。

root: 拉丁语 centrum（中心）→ central → centralize

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers both authority and physical stock moving to one centre.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词既指权威也指实物收拢到一个中心。
